The nonzero dihedral angle, a geometric degree of freedom absent in triatomic reactions, leads to reduced reactivity and enhances sideward scattering for the perpendicular configuration, while leaving the product rovibrational state distributions essentially unchanged. In addition, the alignment of the HD rotational angular momentum is preserved in the rotational direction of the product H 2 O.

summary_en: Examines the US healthcare system's ability to identify and treat perinatal mental illnesses. Proposes improvements and advocates for system changes.

方法亮点：以产后精神病为例
关键发现：呼吁系统变革
insights_en: Novelty: Focuses on the identification and treatment system for perinatal mental illnesses
Method highlight: Uses postpartum psychosis as an example
Key finding: Advocates for system changes
abstract: This Viewpoint, using postpartum psychosis (PPP) as an example, raises questions about the ability of the US health care system to identify and treat perinatal mental illnesses; highlights recent progress and suggests ways to further improve; and calls for system changes to ensure that all patients with perinatal mental illnesses are identified and treated.

RSMViewer: A PyMOL plugin for RNA structural motif visualization
summary_zh: 提出RSMViewer插件，用于RNA结构基序可视化。简化基序探索，提高效率。
summary_en: Introduces RSMViewer plugin for RNA structural motif visualization. Simplifies motif exploration and improves efficiency.
insights: 创新点：开发RNA基序可视化工具
方法亮点：集成异构基序注释
关键发现：提高RNA基序分析效率
insights_en: Novelty: Develops a tool for RNA motif visualization
Method highlight: Integrates heterogeneous motif annotations
Key finding: Improves efficiency of RNA motif analysis
abstract: SUMMARY: RNA structural motifs (RSMs) are recurrent three-dimensional RNA structural elements characterized by conserved three-dimensional geometries and often associated with specific molecular functions. Their identification, validation, and functional characterization frequently require labor-intensive manual inspection. However, existing molecular visualization tools provide limited support for motif-centric exploration, making large-scale visualization and comparative analysis of RNA motifs inefficient and time-consuming. To address this limitation, we present RSMViewer, an open-source PyMOL plug-in that integrates heterogeneous motif annotations and supports batch visualization and efficient structural superimposition of RNA motif instances. RSMViewer streamlines the exploration and comparative analysis of RNA structural motifs, substantially reducing manual effort and facilitating downstream structural and functional interpretation. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: RSMViewer is implemented in Python and is freely available at https://github.com/Rakib-Hasan-Rahad/RSMViewer.git. It is compatible with PyMOL 2.x and later, on all major operating systems. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: Anthropic bought this one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?
Proposed approach for diagnosing obesity outperforms old method
summary_zh: 提出一种基于腰围和相关指标的新框架，通过器官功能障碍区分临床和亚临床肥胖，优于传统BMI标准。
summary_en: A new framework based on waist circumference and related measures distinguishes clinical from preclinical obesity, outperforming conventional BMI criteria.
insights: 创新点：结合腰围和器官功能指标诊断肥胖
方法亮点：多队列研究验证新框架的有效性
关键发现：新框架在诊断肥胖和分层死亡率风险方面优于传统方法
insights_en: Novelty: Combining waist circumference and organ function metrics for obesity diagnosis
Method highlight: Multi-cohort study validates the effectiveness of the new framework
Key finding: The new framework outperforms traditional methods in diagnosing obesity and stratifying mortality risk
abstract: A framework for diagnosing obesity that was proposed in 2025 incorporates waist circumference and related measures and distinguishes clinical from preclinical obesity on the basis of obesity-induced organ dysfunction. In an international multi-cohort study of 844,108 adults, this framework outperformed conventional body-mass-index-based criteria in diagnosing obesity and stratifying mortality risk. A combination of body and organ-function metrics does better at classifying obesity than does body mass index.

title: Normalized membrane ratio of TROP2 as a predictor of clinical outcomes with datopotamab deruxtecan in non-small-cell lung cancer
summary_zh: 开发TROP2定量连续评分方法，通过肿瘤细胞膜和细胞质中的TROP2表达预测临床结果。
summary_en: A TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring method is developed to predict clinical outcomes based on TROP2 expression in tumor cell membranes and cytoplasm.
insights: 创新点：提出TROP2定量连续评分方法
方法亮点：结合免疫组化和计算病理学
关键发现：TROP2表达预测非小细胞肺癌治疗反应
insights_en: Novelty: Proposing the TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring method
Method highlight: Combining immunohistochemistry with computational pathology
Key finding: TROP2 expression predicts treatment response in non-small-cell lung cancer
abstract: Abstract Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd)—a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody–drug conjugate—has demonstrated efficacy in patients with advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ± actionable genomic alterations. However, TROP2 expression by pathologist assessment using conventional immunohistochemistry with visual scoring does not predict response to TROP2-directed antibody–drug conjugates in NSCLC. We developed TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring (QCS)—a fully supervised computational pathology approach that quantifies TROP2 expression in individual NSCLC cells and subcellular components from immunohistochemistry-stained slides. Using QCS to determine TROP2 expression at the tumor cell membrane and cytoplasm, normalized membrane ratio (NMR) was developed (ratio of membrane relative to membrane + cytoplasmic TROP2) in the biomarker-evaluable population of patients with advanced NSCLC in the TROPION-PanTumor01 study ( n = 115). The TROP2 NMR cut-point was optimized and validated in patients with nonsquamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations (primary intended-use population, n = 221) in the biomarker-evaluable population ( n = 352) of the TROPION-Lung01 trial. Association with clinical outcomes was assessed. Progression-free survival was longer in Dato-DXd-treated (median 7.2 versus 4.0 months; hazard ratio 0.40, 95% confidence interval 0.25–0.64) but not docetaxel-treated (median 4.1 versus 4.4 months; hazard ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.59–1.49) patients with TROP2 NMR-positive versus TROP2 NMR-negative samples (treatment by biomarker status interaction P = 0.0098), indicating that TROP2 NMR may be a predictive biomarker for Dato-DXd.

title: Lessons from recent investigator-initiated trials of gene-editing therapies in China
Principles of use of tensile J-curve materials in antagonistic arrangements
summary_zh: 研究J形曲线材料在机器人机制中的应用，以实现软连接和刚性保护。
summary_en: This study investigates the application of tensile J-curve materials in robotic mechanisms to achieve soft connectivity and rigid protection.
insights: 创新点：探索J形曲线材料在机器人中的应用
方法亮点：分析非线性拉伸响应
关键发现：J形曲线材料实现软连接和刚性保护
insights_en: Novelty: Exploring the application of J-curve materials in robotics
Method highlight: Analyzing nonlinear tensile response
Key finding: J-curve materials achieve soft connectivity and rigid protection
abstract: Natural ligaments are soft connective tissues that provide high stretchability for dexterous flexibility but switch to high stiffness to protect the musculoskeletal system from excessive deformation. These two functions cannot be independently tuned in conventional engineering materials with linear or hyperelasticity. Biological materials achieve this tailored behavior through a highly nonlinear tensile response characterized by a J-shaped curve, featuring an extended “toe region” of low force up to intermediate strains followed by an inflection, called the “heel region” which marks the onset of nonlinear stiffening. Here, we aim to study the characteristics of J-curves to establish principles for their use in robotic mechanisms. We define and measure the J-curve features responsible for protectiveness and mobility, describe the effective stiffness and the level of nonlinearity as a function of pre-stretch, and elucidate how the J-curve decouples flexibility from damage protection. Experimental measurements reveal the performance advantages of twisted and coiled elastomeric J-curve materials in engineered antagonistic arrangements and highlight their unique design space compared with linear elastic systems. Furthermore, we present a conceptual analysis of exploiting J-curve materials in energy-efficient running as an outlook toward their use in bioinspired robots.

title: Intermittent Cauchy walks enable optimal 3D search across target shapes and sizes
summary_zh: 分析间歇性Cauchy行走，证明其在不同目标形状和尺寸的3D搜索中是近最优的。
summary_en: Analyzing intermittent Cauchy walks, it is proven that they are near-optimal for 3D search across a wide range of target shapes and sizes.
insights: 创新点：提出间歇性Cauchy行走进行3D搜索
方法亮点：分析目标几何形状对搜索效率的影响
关键发现：Cauchy行走在不同目标形状中表现优异
insights_en: Novelty: Proposing intermittent Cauchy walks for 3D search
Method highlight: Analyzing the impact of target geometry on search efficiency
Key finding: Cauchy walks perform exceptionally well across a wide range of target shapes
abstract: Efficiently locating rare targets requires balancing the exploration of novel space with the exploitation of local vicinities. While this tradeoff is well documented in simplified environments, its behavior in realistic three-dimensional environments remains unclear. Here, we analyze intermittent Lévy walks in three dimensions and show that search efficiency becomes strongly dependent on target geometry, with volume, surface area, and elongation governing performance across the Lévy spectrum. Against this geometric complexity, the Cauchy walk ( μ = 2 ) emerges as a robust, near-optimal solution across a wide range of target geometries. Specifically, we prove that for convex targets of surface area Δ in a domain of volume n , the optimal expected detection time scales as n / Δ , and that the Cauchy walk achieves this scaling up to polylogarithmic factors, while other Lévy strategies are suboptimal in different geometric regimes. Our findings provide a theoretical framework for biological movement patterns, including marine predator foraging and immune surveillance, and inform the design of efficient search algorithms for engineered systems such as autonomous nanoscale explorers.

title: Dormancy stabilizes structured food webs
summary_zh: 研究预测物种间强互动导致生态系统不稳定，但强互动在自然界普遍存在，强不稳定性却罕见。休眠可能是一种限制或对抗不稳定的生态机制。休眠个体形成‘种子库’，暂时脱离种群过程和物种互动，记录过去生态动态。种子库可稳定捕食者-猎物互动，但其对更大生态网络稳定性的影响尚不明确。
summary_en: The theory predicts that strong species interactions drive instability in large ecosystems, but strong interactions are common in nature while strong instability appears rare. Dormancy, a reversible metabolic suppression, may be one ecological mechanism that limits or counters instability. Dormant individuals form 'seed banks' that are temporarily disengaged from demographic processes and species interactions, recording past ecological dynamics. Seed banks can stabilize predator-prey interactions, but whether, when, and how they affect the stability of larger ecological networks is uncertain.
insights: 创新点：休眠作为生态稳定性机制的新发现
方法亮点：种子库对生态网络稳定性的影响研究
关键发现：休眠个体通过种子库影响生态网络稳定性
insights_en: Novelty: The discovery of dormancy as a new ecological stability mechanism
Method highlight: The study of the impact of seed banks on the stability of ecological networks
Key finding: Dormant individuals affect the stability of ecological networks through seed banks
abstract: Theory predicts that strong species interactions drive instability in large ecosystems, but strong interactions are common in nature while strong instability appears rare. This discrepancy motivates enduring interest in ecological mechanisms that limit or counteract instability. Dormancy—reversible metabolic suppression—may be one. Dormancy is a ubiquitous life history trait found in organisms ranging from bacteria to trees. Dormant individuals form “seed banks” that are temporarily disengaged from demographic processes and species interactions, creating a memory of past ecological dynamics. Seed banks can stabilize predator–prey interactions, but whether, when, and how they affect the stability of larger ecological networks is uncertain. We show that dormancy stabilizes oscillatory dynamics in a minimal mathematical model and illustrate how dormancy converts high oscillation frequency into strong restoring force. We find that dormancy can have qualitative stabilizing effects in structured food webs that undergo Hopf bifurcations and exhibit oscillatory instability, but rarely in unstructured networks or networks with symmetric (competitive or mutualistic) interactions. This classification remains accurate when only some species go dormant and drive stabilization. Our results clarify when dormancy can promote stability, indicating that it may be an important but overlooked stabilizing factor in food webs.

title: RE1 silencing transcription factor is reduced in endometriosis, and uterine deletion in mice alters progesterone responsiveness
summary_zh: 子宫内膜异位症是一种激素依赖性妇科疾病，表现为孕酮抵抗、不孕/不育和盆腔疼痛。本研究通过人类组织和小鼠模型，探讨了RE1沉默转录因子（REST）在子宫内膜异位症中的作用。研究发现，子宫内膜异位症患者中REST表达显著降低，提示其功能丧失。
summary_en: Endometriosis is a hormone-dependent gynecological disease characterized by progesterone resistance, subfertility/infertility, and pelvic pain. This study investigates the role of RE1 silencing transcription factor (REST) in endometriosis using human tissues and a uterine-specific Rest conditional knockout mouse model. The study found that nuclear REST expression was significantly reduced in patients with endometriosis, suggesting a loss of function.
insights: 创新点：REST在子宫内膜异位症中的作用研究
方法亮点：人类组织和小鼠模型的应用
关键发现：子宫内膜异位症患者REST表达降低
insights_en: Novelty: The study of the role of REST in endometriosis
Method highlight: The application of human tissues and mouse models
Key finding: Reduced REST expression in endometriosis patients
abstract: Endometriosis is a steroid-dependent gynecologic disease characterized by progesterone (P4) resistance, subfertility/infertility, and pelvic pain; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying impaired P4 responsiveness in endometriosis tissue are not fully understood. RE1 silencing transcription factor (REST), a transcriptional regulator implicated in steroid hormone signaling, has emerged as a potential mediator of P4 responsiveness. Here, we investigated the role of REST in endometriosis using human tissues and a uterine-specific Rest conditional knockout mouse model. Immunohistochemical analysis of eutopic endometrium and ectopic lesions from patients with endometriosis revealed significantly reduced nuclear REST expression compared with control endometrium, suggesting loss of functional REST in disease. To assess the physiological consequences of REST deficiency, uterine-specific Rest knockout (Rest d/d ) mice were generated. Rest d/d females exhibited progressive subfertility and hyperestrogenic uterine tissue characteristics that displayed a blunted responsiveness to P4 treatment. Loss of Rest selectively altered expression of P4-responsive genes associated with endometriosis pathology, despite preserved P4 receptor expression. Following induction of experimental endometriosis, female mice that developed endometriotic-like lesions using Rest-deficient donor tissue developed significantly larger lesions that were less responsive to P4 treatment compared to lesions induced using control tissue. Mechanical sensitivity was modestly increased in mice receiving Rest-deficient tissue, whereas vaginal hyperalgesia was unaffected. These findings identify loss of nuclear REST as a feature of endometriosis and support a role of REST in subfertility, lesion progression, and blunted response to P4. REST may represent a molecular contributor to altered P4 responsiveness and a potential therapeutic target in endometriosis.

title: Multi-omics characterization of white matter free water reveals genetic and vascular determinants of neurological disorders
summary_zh: 本研究通过多组学方法，对42,039名个体的白质自由水（FW-WM）进行特征化分析，揭示了其遗传和血管决定因素。研究发现，与传统的白质指标相比，20个位点（74%）是新的，表明遗传易感性和FW-WM水平与神经系统疾病相关。
summary_en: This study conducted a multi-omics analysis of white matter free water (FW-WM) in 42,039 individuals, revealing genetic and vascular determinants of neurological disorders. The study found that 20 loci (74%) were novel compared to conventional white matter metrics, indicating a genetic predisposition to higher FW-WM levels and their association with neurological disorders.
insights: 创新点：白质自由水与神经系统疾病关联的新发现
方法亮点：多组学方法的应用
关键发现：新的遗传位点与白质自由水相关
insights_en: Novelty: The new discovery of the association between white matter free water and neurological disorders
Method highlight: The application of multi-omics methods
Key finding: Novel genetic loci associated with white matter free water
abstract: White matter free water (FW-WM), quantified using diffusion MRI, reflects extracellular water content and microstructural alterations within water matter, but its genetic architecture and clinical relevance remain largely uncharted. We conducted a multi-omics study integrating 42,039 individuals from the UK Biobank and Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative cohorts to characterize tract-specific FW-WM across genetic, phenotypic, and proteomic dimensions. Genome-wide association analyses identified 27 independent loci and prioritized 88 genes, which were enriched in the genomic functional elements of vascular endothelial cells, pericytes, and astrocytes. Notably, 20 loci (74%) were novel compared to conventional white matter metrics. Both genetic predisposition to higher FW-WM and imaging-derived FW-WM were associated with a spectrum of neurological disorders. Specifically, imaging-derived FW-WM showed strong associations with stroke (OR = 3.14) and dementia (OR = 4.15), while higher baseline FW-WM predicted progression from MCI to AD (HR = 2.58). Bidirectional Mendelian randomization analyses further supported genetically predicted associations between hypertension and FW-WM, which were together associated with increased risks of stroke and cognitive impairment. Integrative proteomic analyses further nominated PEAR1 and ANGL3 as candidate proteins potentially linking hypertension-related vascular processes to FW-WM variation. Together, these findings provide a multi-omics characterization of FW-WM that connects genetic susceptibility, vascular factors, and neurological outcomes, supporting FW-WM as a tract-specific imaging phenotype with potential utility for neurological risk stratification.

title: Phase transition in a dryland shrub–grass ecosystem: Emergence through local trade-offs
summary_zh: 本研究将相变理论应用于干旱地区灌木-草地生态系统，发现这些系统表现出相变的三个特征：不同生态阶段的急剧转变、灌木草原和草原之间的多稳态，以及临界转变。
summary_en: This study applies phase transition theory to dryland shrub-grass ecosystems, finding that these systems exhibit three hallmarks of phase transitions: abrupt shifts between different ecological phases, multistability between shrublands and grasslands, and critical transitions.
insights: 创新点：相变理论在生态系统中的应用
方法亮点：结合实证证据与理论分析
关键发现：干旱生态系统中的相变特征
insights_en: Novelty: The application of phase transition theory to ecosystems
Method highlight: The combination of empirical evidence and theoretical analysis
Key finding: Phase transition characteristics in dryland ecosystems
abstract: Ecosystems are complex adaptive systems in which local interactions among individuals shape macroscopic phenomena such as pattern formation, multistability, and critical transitions. However, how such bottom-up interactions govern emergent behaviors and system-level complexity remains a central challenge in ecology. Phase transition theory, a classic paradigm in physics, links local interaction rules to emergent changes in macroscopic system states, offering a formal language for understanding cross-scale dynamics. Here we unite this theory with empirical evidence from dryland shrub–grass ecosystems and show that these systems exhibit three hallmarks of phase transitions. First, abrupt shifts separate different phases of deserts, shrublands, and grasslands. Second, shrublands and grasslands self-organize into Turing-like phase patterns, contrasting with homogeneous deserts. Third, special phenomena emerge near-transition threshold, including patch enlargement and abrupt decline at desert–vegetation interface, and fairy circles within the shrub–grass transition zone. Using a cellular automaton model built on a fundamental trade-off between extensive and intensive resource foraging strategies (EI trade-off), we show how kernels encoding local trade-offs integrate these seemingly disparate phenomena within a unified phase transition framework. Moreover, this EI trade-off was empirically validated through analyses of plant functional traits and spatial patterns of plant patches. These findings illustrate that dryland ecosystem dynamics reflect universal self-organization principles. Our work establishes phase-transition theory as a powerful framework for understanding, predicting, and managing complexity in dryland ecosystems, which advances the integration of complexity science with ecology, offering a pathway toward bottom-up ecosystem understanding.

title: PPP1R1B differentially modulates alcohol intake and emotional comorbidity through distinct prefrontal circuits
summary_zh: 本研究通过化学遗传学、逆向追踪、电生理学、空间蛋白质组学和细胞特异性基因编辑等方法，研究了PPP1R1B在酒精摄入和情绪共病中的作用。研究发现，PPP1R1B通过不同的前额叶回路调节酒精摄入和情绪共病。
summary_en: This study investigates the role of PPP1R1B in alcohol intake and emotional comorbidity using methods such as chemogenetics, retrograde tracing, electrophysiology, spatial proteomics, and cell-type-specific gene editing. The study found that PPP1R1B modulates alcohol intake and emotional comorbidity through distinct prefrontal circuits.
insights: 创新点：PPP1R1B在酒精摄入和情绪共病中的作用研究
方法亮点：多种神经科学技术的综合应用
关键发现：PPP1R1B通过不同回路调节酒精摄入和情绪共病
insights_en: Novelty: The study of the role of PPP1R1B in alcohol intake and emotional comorbidity
Method highlight: The comprehensive application of various neuroscience technologies
Key finding: PPP1R1B modulates alcohol intake and emotional comorbidity through distinct circuits
abstract: Excessive alcohol consumption frequently co-occurs with anxiety and depression in alcohol use disorder (AUD), yet the specific neural circuits and molecular mechanisms coordinating these comorbid conditions remain poorly defined. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), particularly its prelimbic (PL) and infralimbic (IL) subregions, projects to key reward and emotion centers like the nucleus accumbens (Nac) and basolateral amygdala (BLA), but the functional heterogeneity of these projections is unclear. Using chemogenetics, retrograde tracing, electrophysiology, spatial proteomics, and cell-type-specific gene editing in mice subjected to a 4-wk intermittent access to alcohol (IAA) paradigm, we selectively manipulated glutamatergic projections from the PL and IL to the Nac core, Nac shell, and BLA and assessed alcohol intake, anxiety-like, and depression-like behaviors. Chemogenetic activation of PL-Nac core projections reduced short-term alcohol intake, anxiety-, and depression-like behaviors, while IL-BLA activation decreased alcohol consumption and anxiety-like behaviors only. Retrograde tracing revealed mirror-image anatomical segregation of projection-defined neuronal subpopulations within PL/IL linking spatial organization to functional divergence. IAA induced pathway-specific synaptic adaptations. Spatial proteomics nominated protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a candidate molecule in PL-Nac core neurons. Independent immunostaining confirmed PPP1R1B downregulation, and circuit-specific knockout recapitulated alcohol-related and affective phenotypes, whereas overexpression reversed them. In IL-BLA neurons, PPP1R1B manipulation modulated alcohol intake and anxiety, but not depression. These findings define a subregion- and projection-specific organizational logic in the mPFC for differentially regulating alcohol consumption and emotional comorbidity, with PPP1R1B as a key molecular determinant. This provides a neural pathway–molecule framework for targeted intervention in AUD.

title: Phylogenetic profiling reveals evolutionary coupling between methyltransferases and the cytoskeleton
summary_zh: 本研究通过全人类甲基转移酶谱的进化分析，揭示了甲基转移酶与细胞骨架之间的进化耦合关系。研究发现，甲基转移酶与细胞骨架蛋白的甲基化修饰广泛存在，表明甲基化在细胞骨架组织中的重要作用。
summary_en: This study, through phylogenetic profiling of the complete repertoire of human methyltransferases, reveals an evolutionary coupling between methyltransferases and the cytoskeleton. The study found that methyltransferases are widely involved in the methylation modification of cytoskeletal proteins, indicating the important role of methylation in cytoskeletal organization.
insights: 创新点：甲基转移酶与细胞骨架进化耦合关系的新发现
方法亮点：全人类甲基转移酶谱的进化分析
关键发现：甲基化在细胞骨架组织中的重要作用
insights_en: Novelty: The new discovery of the evolutionary coupling between methyltransferases and the cytoskeleton
Method highlight: The evolutionary analysis of the complete repertoire of human methyltransferases
Key finding: The important role of methylation in cytoskeletal organization
abstract: Methylation is a fundamental post-translational modification best understood as regulating chromatin structure and gene expression, yet there is emerging evidence that methylation also shapes cytoskeletal organization, regulating key processes such as mitosis and cell migration. Proteomic studies have revealed cytoskeletal protein methylation is widespread, however little is known about the enzymes responsible for these modifications, or their evolutionary relationship to other, better known substrates for methylation, such as chromatin. To address this question, we applied phylogenetic profiling across the complete repertoire of human methyltransferases to identify conserved functional relationships extending beyond chromatin. Unbiased clustering revealed extensive coevolution between methyltransferases and many components of the cytoskeleton, uncovering a previously unrecognized evolutionary network linking canonical chromatin regulatory enzymes to cellular structural systems. Evolutionary Trace analysis of the H3K36 methyltransferase family recovered known catalytic and regulatory domains while identifying additional evolutionarily constrained residues, suggesting previously unappreciated functional interfaces. Comparative analyses further distinguished deeply conserved methyltransferase–cytoskeletal relationships from those that emerged later during eukaryotic evolution, indicating that cytoskeletal methylation comprises both ancient and lineage-expanded regulatory programs. Leveraging these evolutionary signatures, we identified and experimentally validated a previously unrecognized association between the methyltransferase NSD3 and α-tubulin. Together, these findings reveal that methyltransferases traditionally viewed as chromatin regulators participate in an evolutionarily conserved network that coordinates nuclear and cytoskeletal functions. More broadly, they establish phylogenetic profiling as a powerful approach for discovering noncanonical activities of chromatin-associated enzymes and suggest that regulation of chromatin organization and cellular architecture evolved as interconnected processes.

title: Correction for Ge et al., Empirical validation of race-neutral normative brain morphometry models across ethnoracially diverse populations
Structural insights into the evolution of mitochondrial protein import from the trypanosome ATOM complex
summary_zh: 本研究报告了非洲锥虫ATOM复合物的冷冻电镜结构，揭示了其与真核生物TOM复合物的保守性。尽管组成不同，ATOM保留了保守的二聚通道结构和蛋白质传导途径，表明其核心机制与真核生物TOM复合物相似。
summary_en: This study reports the cryo-electron microscopy structure of the Trypanosoma brucei ATOM complex, revealing its conservation with eukaryotic TOM complexes. Despite its divergent composition, ATOM retains a conserved dimeric channel architecture and a protein-conducting pathway closely resembling those of eukaryotic TOM complexes, indicating that the core mechanism is similar to that of eukaryotic TOM complexes.
insights: 创新点：非洲锥虫ATOM复合物的结构解析
方法亮点：冷冻电镜技术的应用
关键发现：ATOM与真核生物TOM复合物的保守性
insights_en: Novelty: The structural elucidation of the Trypanosoma brucei ATOM complex
Method highlight: The application of cryo-electron microscopy
Key finding: The conservation of ATOM with eukaryotic TOM complexes
abstract: The translocase of the outer membrane (TOM) mediates the import of most mitochondrial preproteins. In the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma brucei , this machinery is replaced by the atypical translocase of the outer membrane (ATOM), whose composition differs substantially from the canonical TOM complexes of fungi and metazoans. Here, we report the cryoelectron microscopy structure of the T. brucei ATOM complex at 2.8 Å resolution. The structure resolves all previously identified components together with an additional, previously uncharacterized subunit. Despite its divergent composition, ATOM retains a conserved dimeric channel architecture and a protein-conducting pathway closely resembling those of opisthokont TOM complexes, indicating that the core mechanism of mitochondrial protein translocation was established early in eukaryotic evolution. In contrast, the receptor and intermembrane-space regions exhibit distinct architectures, revealing extensive evolutionary diversification and multiple examples of convergent evolution. Together, these findings provide a near-atomic view of the ATOM translocase and offer insights into the origin, conservation, and diversification of the mitochondrial protein import machinery across eukaryotes.

title: Physiologic and pharmacologic role of the glucocorticoid receptor in germinal center B cells and plasmacytic differentiation
summary_zh: 本研究通过GC特异性Nr3c1敲除小鼠模型和多组学分析，揭示了糖皮质激素受体（GR）在GC B细胞和浆细胞分化中的生理和药理作用。研究发现，GR在生理条件下定位于细胞核，通过转录调控信号通路，部分通过拮抗BCL6对浆细胞主调节因子的抑制功能，调节GC稳态和浆细胞分化。
summary_en: This study, using a GC-specific Nr3c1 knockout mouse model and multi-omics analyses, reveals the physiological and pharmacological role of the glucocorticoid receptor (GR) in germinal center B cells and plasmacytic differentiation. The study found that GR is constitutively localized to the nucleus under physiological conditions, modulating signaling pathways implicated in GC homeostasis and plasmablast differentiation, in part by antagonizing the repressive function of BCL6 on the plasma cell master regulator.
insights: 创新点：GR在GC B细胞和浆细胞分化中的作用研究
方法亮点：GC特异性Nr3c1敲除小鼠模型和多组学分析
关键发现：GR调节GC稳态和浆细胞分化
insights_en: Novelty: The study of the role of GR in germinal center B cells and plasmacytic differentiation
Method highlight: The application of a GC-specific Nr3c1 knockout mouse model and multi-omics analyses
Key finding: GR modulates GC homeostasis and plasmacytic differentiation
abstract: In diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL), a malignancy derived from germinal center (GC) B cells, somatic hypermutation aberrantly targets glucocorticoid receptor (GR) binding sequences in the super-enhancer (SE) of multiple oncogenes. These events abrogate GR binding and deregulate the expression of the SE-linked gene, suggesting an important role of GR in normal and transformed GC B cells. Using a GC-specific Nr3c1 knockout mouse model and multi-omics analyses in murine and human GC B cells, here we show that, under physiological conditions, GR constitutively localizes to the nucleus, where it transcriptionally modulates signaling pathways implicated in GC homeostasis and plasmablast differentiation in part by antagonizing the repressive function of BCL6 on the plasma cell master regulators IRF4 and PRDM1. While loss of baseline GR activity led to mild GC hyperplasia and impaired plasmacytic differentiation, pharmacologic doses of glucocorticoids, a key component of DLBCL chemo-immunotherapy, were preferentially toxic to GC in a GC B cell–autonomous manner. These findings uncover a physiological role for GR in the GC reaction as well as in promoting plasmablast/plasma cell formation and provide insights into the specific activity of glucocorticoids in the treatment of DLBCL.

title: Modest loss of sleep increases susceptibility to cybersecurity threats
summary_zh: 研究睡眠不足如何影响认知处理，发现时差调整后点击可疑链接概率上升13%。实验未影响打开邮件或标记为垃圾邮件的概率。
summary_en: The study examines how sleep deprivation affects cognitive processing, finding a 13% increase in the likelihood of clicking on suspicious links after daylight saving time adjustment, without affecting email opening or spam reporting.
insights: 创新点：首次将时差调整与网络钓鱼攻击联系起来
方法亮点：采用自然实验和随机分配
关键发现：睡眠不足显著增加网络钓鱼攻击风险
insights_en: Novelty: First to link daylight saving time adjustment with phishing attacks
Method highlight: Employed a naturalistic experiment with random assignment
Key finding: Sleep deprivation significantly increases the risk of phishing attacks
abstract: Sleep restriction leads to impaired cognitive processing across domains. I examined whether the transition to daylight saving time (DST), typically accompanied by compromised sleep, would lead to an increase in the probability of falling prey to a simulated phishing attack using a fully naturalistic experiment with random assignment and blinding. A predatory email was sent to employees at the University of California, Irvine (N = 11,218) either on the morning of Monday following the transition to DST or one week earlier. The transition led to a ~13% increase in the probability of clicking a suspicious link, without affecting the probability of opening the email or reporting it as spam. These results demonstrate that even modest, mundane, and acute loss of sleep has real-life, potentially hazardous, implications for cognitive function.

title: Phosphatases regulating ERK activation and ERK-dependent cell migration
summary_zh: 研究ERK磷酸酶，发现EYA家族磷酸酶是ERK信号的关键调节因子，并在果蝇和哺乳动物细胞中发挥重要作用。
summary_en: The study investigates ERK phosphatases, finding that EYA family phosphatases are critical regulators of ERK signaling and play a significant role in both Drosophila and mammalian cells.
insights: 创新点：揭示了EYA家族磷酸酶在ERK信号中的关键作用
方法亮点：采用高吞吐量筛选和体内验证方法
关键发现：EYA4抑制在人类细胞中有效
insights_en: Novelty: Revealed the critical role of EYA family phosphatases in ERK signaling
Method highlight: Employed high-throughput screening and in vivo validation methods
Key finding: EYA4 inhibition is effective in human cells
abstract: Extracellular signal-regulated kinases (ERKs) have essential roles in development and are implicated in numerous diseases. ERKs are activated by phosphorylation and are regulated by dephosphorylation. To study the ERK phosphatases, we adapted a method to monitor ERK activity in live, unfixed preparations that accommodates the highly dynamic temporal and spatial features of ERK activation. We evaluated 140 human phosphatases using an in vivo reporter (ERK-SPARK) for high-throughput screening in human cells, and we used an in vivo Drosophila model for functional validation of their phosphatase homologs. We found that EYA family phosphatases are critical regulators of ERK signaling both in Drosophila and in mammalian cells and found that inhibition of human EYA4, a homolog of Drosophila Eyes Absent phosphatase, enhances migration of ERK-responsive tumor cells. These findings have important implications for the development of therapeutics.

title: Lipid droplets buffer hydrogen sulfide–induced redox imbalance
summary_zh: 研究慢性硫化氢暴露对细胞的影响，发现脂滴在调节硫化氢引起的氧化还原失衡中起关键作用。
summary_en: The study investigates the effects of chronic hydrogen sulfide exposure on cells, finding that lipid droplets play a key role in buffering the redox imbalance induced by hydrogen sulfide.
insights: 创新点：发现脂滴在硫化氢暴露中的保护作用
方法亮点：采用脂质组学分析技术
关键发现：硫化氢暴露导致NAD和CoQ池的还原性变化
insights_en: Novelty: Identified the protective role of lipid droplets in hydrogen sulfide exposure
Method highlight: Employed lipidomic analysis techniques
Key finding: Hydrogen sulfide exposure leads to redox changes in NAD and CoQ pools
abstract: The electron transport chain is a signaling hub for hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) that serves both as a respiratory substrate and an inhibitor. While acute sulfide toxicity is well characterized, cellular adaptations to chronic H 2 S, particularly microbially-derived sulfide exposure in colon, is poorly understood. We report that chronic, low-level H 2 S exposure (4 to 20 µM) drives robust carbon sequestration in lipid droplets (LD) across several human cell lines, driven by a coordinated remodeling of redox and nucleotide metabolism. Specifically, H 2 S-induced reductive shifts in nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and coenzyme Q (CoQ) pools are accompanied by glycerol-3-phosphate accumulation and cytidine triphosphate (CTP) depletion. Lipidomic analysis reveals increased neutral lipid synthesis and triacylglyceride accumulation concomitant with decreased CTP-dependent synthesis of membrane phospholipids. Mitochondrial expression of a water-generating NADH oxidase attenuates LD accumulation and spatially confines the origin of H 2 S-induced reductive stress signaling to this compartment. Interestingly, LD abundance increases even after H 2 S withdrawal, continuing over 48 h, during which time the reductively-shifted NAD and CoQ pools slowly reoxidize. Inhibition of fatty acid synthesis during sulfide exposure impairs cellular recovery of respiration. These findings establish an active role for LDs in stress response and reveal that lipid biogenesis is a strategy for countering H 2 S-induced redox imbalance. The sulfide–LD–redox axis uncovered in this study has implications for understanding how gut-derived H 2 S, shaped by diet and microbiome, can influence metabolic health.

title: Wearable interstitial fluid sensing of time-resolved uric acid for early prediction of flare-associated pain in an induced mouse model
summary_zh: 开发了一种可穿戴的间质液尿酸传感器，用于早期预测痛风发作相关的疼痛。
summary_en: A wearable interstitial fluid uric acid sensor for early prediction of pain associated with gout flares in an induced mouse model has been developed.
insights: 创新点：开发了一种新的痛风疼痛预测方法
方法亮点：集成酶传感器和近场通信技术
关键发现：传感器有效监测尿酸动态变化
insights_en: Novelty: Developed a new method for predicting gout pain
Method highlight: Integrated enzyme sensors and near-field communication technology
Key finding: The sensor effectively monitors uric acid dynamics
abstract: Gout flare is driven by hyperuricemia (HUA) and inflammatory responses to monosodium urate (MSU) crystals, yet single time-point serum uric acid (UA) measurements cannot capture the biochemical dynamics preceding flare onset or explain the timing of severe pain manifestation. Here, we present a skin-attachable interstitial fluid (ISF)-based electrochemical sensing platform for time-resolved, minimally invasive UA monitoring in a controlled, induced mouse model of gout flare-associated inflammation and pain. The platform integrates an enzyme-based UA sensor, a thin insertion electrode, and battery-free near-field communication (NFC), enabling time-resolved in vivo tracking of ISF UA dynamics. By establishing disease-stage-specific models comprising HUA, MSU-only inflammation, and gouty arthritis flare (GA flare) conditions, we separately examined metabolic and inflammatory contributions to flare-associated UA dynamics. Time-resolved ISF monitoring revealed that the GA flare group exhibited pronounced UA fluctuation patterns that were not reproduced by either condition alone. The peak timing of UA dynamics was temporally decoupled from pain-related behavioral responses, indicating that flare-associated pain onset cannot be explained by a single UA concentration. A machine learning framework using ISF UA time-series features identified predictive information preceding peak pain, whereas analyses using earlier events defined by sustained decreases in paw withdrawal threshold showed lower and event-definition-dependent performance. These findings establish time-resolved ISF UA monitoring as a framework for resolving flare-associated biochemical dynamics and evaluating subsequent pain progression in an induced mouse model.

title: Correction for Santos et al., Treating language contact as normal: Coalescent-theoretic modeling of the prehistory of the Bantu language family
How Antoni Gaudí used math to make his basilica soar
Young people with obesity deserve better care
Effect of two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens on the gut microbiome in a randomized phase 3 trial
Gut and urogenital microbiomes influence menopausal hormone therapy outcomes
A lactate-fatty acid loop drives prostate cancer bone colonization by mediating metabolic interplay between tumor cells and osteoblasts
summary_zh: 研究发现，乳酸盐-脂肪酸循环通过调节肿瘤细胞和成骨细胞之间的代谢相互作用，驱动前列腺癌细胞骨转移。
summary_en: The study finds that a lactate-fatty acid loop drives prostate cancer bone colonization by mediating metabolic interactions between tumor cells and osteoblasts.
insights: 创新点：发现乳酸盐-脂肪酸循环在骨转移中的作用
方法亮点：研究肿瘤细胞与成骨细胞的代谢相互作用
关键发现：MCT1是乳酸摄取的关键转运蛋白
insights_en: Novelty: Discovery of the role of the lactate-fatty acid loop in bone metastasis
Method highlight: Studying metabolic interactions between tumor cells and osteoblasts
Key finding: MCT1 is the essential transporter mediating lactate uptake
abstract: Abstract Bone metastasis is the major cause of morbidity and mortality in advanced prostate cancer, yet current therapies provide only limited clinical benefit. Here, we show that prostate cancer cells metabolically adapt to the bone microenvironment by utilizing bone-cell-derived lactate as an alternative nutrient source. Beyond fueling oxidative phosphorylation, lactate serves as carbon source for fatty acid synthesis. Among the resulting lipid products, oleic acid is secreted to reward osteoblast, establishing a reciprocal metabolic interplay that supports both tumor progression and pathological bone formation. Mechanistically, we identify MCT1 as the essential transporter mediating lactate uptake in bone-colonizing tumor cells. MCT1 expression is coordinately regulated by NFAT signaling and extracellular glucose availability at both transcriptional and post-translational levels. Genetic deletion and pharmacological inhibition of MCT1 markedly suppresses prostate tumor growth in bone. Together, these findings uncover a lactate-driven metabolic crosstalk, identifying MCT1 as a promising therapeutic target for prostate cancer bone metastasis.

title: Toward personalized deep brain stimulation via white matter stimulation and microstructure in depression
summary_zh: 研究通过分析患者白质微结构和刺激模型，探索个性化深部脑刺激治疗抑郁症。
summary_en: The study explores personalized deep brain stimulation for depression by analyzing patient white matter microstructure and stimulation models.
insights: 创新点：个性化深部脑刺激治疗抑郁症的新方法
方法亮点：结合白质微结构和刺激模型
关键发现：白质微结构影响治疗反应
insights_en: Novelty: New method for personalized deep brain stimulation in depression
Method highlight: Combining white matter microstructure and stimulation models
Key finding: White matter microstructure affects treatment response
abstract: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) affects a substantial proportion of individuals with major depressive disorder, posing a significant clinical and societal burden. Among emerging interventions, tractography-guided Subcallosal Cingulate Deep Brain Stimulation (SCC-DBS) shows promise as a treatment for TRD. However, despite the use of connectome-based targeting methods, clinical outcomes remain variable across individuals. Here, we examined individual white matter (WM) properties underlying the variability of SCC-DBS response for depression by analyzing a patient-specific diffusion MRI dataset of SCC-DBS patients (n = 51), incorporating individualized stimulation modeling and weekly clinical assessments over the first 24 weeks of DBS. We evaluated two distinct WM measures: the volumetric proportion of stimulated WM tracts (STP: stimulated-tract proportion) and the microstructural integrity of these tracts estimated by fractional anisotropy (FA). The STP in the bilateral mid-cingulum bundles and forceps minor reaching the left ventral frontal pole was positively associated with clinical improvement. Although FA alone did not show association with clinical improvement, it moderated the relationship between STP and clinical improvement, suggesting differential contributions of the two pathways in mediating antidepressant effects of SCC-DBS. These findings underscore that future refinements in stimulation delivery may be guided by greater attention to patient-specific WM metrics within the targeted network. A study of 51 patients receiving deep brain stimulation for treatment-resistant depression shows that individual white matter stimulation and integrity jointly influence antidepressant response, supporting more personalized neuromodulation strategies.

title: Temporal dynamics of premenstrual dysphoric disorder revealed through predictive symptom networks
summary_zh: 研究通过预测症状网络揭示经前期焦虑症的时间动态变化。
summary_en: The study reveals the temporal dynamics of premenstrual dysphoric disorder through predictive symptom networks.
insights: 创新点：经前期焦虑症时间动态研究的新方法
方法亮点：预测症状网络的应用
关键发现：个体症状时间模式差异
insights_en: Novelty: New method for studying the temporal dynamics of premenstrual dysphoric disorder
Method highlight: Application of predictive symptom networks
Key finding: Individual differences in symptom timing patterns
abstract: Temporal dynamics of psychiatric symptoms challenge researchers and clinicians due to their inherent unpredictability. The cyclical on-off nature of symptoms linked to physiological rhythms, such as the menstrual cycle, provides a unique window to apply temporal and dynamic modeling of psychiatric symptoms. This can be studied in premenstrual dysphoric disorder, a female hormone-triggered condition characterized by cyclical symptoms. Yet intra-individual temporal patterns and dynamics of these symptoms remain unknown. Here we show that individuals with premenstrual dysphoric disorder differ widely in symptom timing, severity, and persistence, clustering into distinct temporal symptom profiles. Dynamic modelling uncovers temporal order among core psychiatric symptoms, with anxiety emerging as a central symptom in the unfolding of affective dysregulation. Depression shows the strongest predictive associations with subsequent severity of the other core symptoms, while irritability predicts the severity of depression at the longest time-interval. These temporal symptom dynamics reveal mechanistic psychoneuroendocrine pathways and inform precision, time-sensitive interventions for the mental health of individuals with premenstrual dysphoric disorder.

title: Frequency-tagged fMRI reveals dual mechanisms of attentional enhancement and suppression
summary_zh: 研究利用频率标记fMRI揭示注意力如何影响视觉刺激的时空动态。发现不同皮层区域表现出同步或反同步，增强目标或抑制周围视觉。注意力增强普遍提高周围抑制。
summary_en: This study uses frequency-tagged fMRI to reveal how attention shapes the spatiotemporal dynamics of visual stimuli. Different cortical regions exhibit either in-phase or anti-phase synchronization, enhancing the target or suppressing the surrounding visual field. Directed attention uniformly enhances surround suppression.
insights: 创新点：频率标记fMRI用于研究注意力机制
方法亮点：揭示注意力对视觉刺激的时空影响
关键发现：注意力增强普遍提高周围抑制
insights_en: Novelty: Frequency-tagged fMRI for studying attention mechanisms
Method highlight: Revealing the temporal-spatial impact of attention on visual stimuli
Key finding: Directed attention uniformly enhances surround suppression
abstract: Selective attention biases competition between concurrent visual inputs, yet its computational implementation in the human cortex remains unclear. Using frequency-tagged fMRI (ft-fMRI), we resolve how attention shapes the spatiotemporal dynamics of competing stimulus-driven responses at fine spatial scales. Distinct cortical populations exhibit either in-phase synchronization (target enhancement) or anti-phase synchronization (surround suppression) with attended stimuli. Population receptive field mapping reveals a target–surround organization, with in-phase populations biased toward the attended target and anti-phase populations biased toward the surrounding visual field. Directed attention uniformly amplifies surround suppression across the visual hierarchy, consistent with a distributed suppressive field, whereas modulation of target-related activity increases hierarchically from V1 to hV4. Critically, modulation of surround suppression, but not target enhancement, predicts behavioral performance. These findings dissociate the mechanisms of target enhancement and surround suppression and reveal the computational architecture underlying biased competition in the human cortex, converging with recent primate electrophysiology research. Rafeh et al. use frequency-tagged fMRI to demonstrate that selective attention relies on dual, independent neural mechanisms for target enhancement and surround suppression, elaborating on traditional unitary models of human visual attention.

title: Topographical mismatch sustains open microchannels in living soft tissue for non-destructive protein biopsy
summary_zh: 通过拓扑不匹配技术，实现软组织中微通道的长期开放，避免炎症，实现非破坏性蛋白质活检。
summary_en: Topographical mismatch technology enables long-term patency of microchannels in living soft tissue, avoiding inflammation for non-destructive protein biopsy.
insights: 创新点：拓扑不匹配技术用于维持微通道开放
方法亮点：实现非炎症性活检
关键发现：微通道长期开放，超过42小时
insights_en: Novelty: Topographical mismatch technology for maintaining microchannel patency
Method highlight: Achieving non-inflammatory biopsy
Key finding: Microchannels remain open for over 42 hours
abstract: Sustaining open microchannels within living soft tissue has remained a problem of mechanics: implants rigid enough to maintain patent channels inflict inflammation, while implants compliant enough to avoid it are sealed within minutes by viscoelastic recoil. Here, we resolve this conflict through topographical mismatch—a deliberate geometric non-conformity between an ultrathin multi-lobed implant and the surrounding tissue. Engineered to exceed the conformability limit of skin, these conduits sustain patency for over 42 hours of sustained physiological deformation and for at least 7 days in living skin without triggering the mechanotransductive signalling that initiates fibrotic encapsulation, and transmit macromolecules of up to 70 kilodaltons through intact skin—surpassing the molecular weight ceiling of transdermal iontophoresis. In vivo, this access reveals that interstitial fluid concentration of a model protein peaks 4.7-fold higher than serum at 2 hours, inverts at 8 hours and rebounds by 24 hours, uncovering tissue-level pharmacokinetics inaccessible to blood sampling. Topographical mismatch establishes a generalisable design principle for sustained, biocompatible interfaces between soft devices and living tissue. Skin-attached devices can easily inflame or collapse. Here, the authors show a multi-lobed microneedle device that holds micron-scale conduits open for seven days, allowing repeated protein sampling from interstitial fluid

title: Functionally divergent RHOA mutations drive peripheral T cell lymphoma development by engaging a common neomorphic pathway
summary_zh: RHOA突变通过激活VAV1-like活性，驱动T细胞淋巴瘤发展，该活性不依赖经典RAS信号。
summary_en: RHOA mutations drive peripheral T-cell lymphoma development by activating a non-canonical VAV1-like activity, independent of the classical RAS signaling.
insights: 创新点：RHOA突变驱动淋巴瘤发展
方法亮点：揭示VAV1-like活性作用
关键发现：不依赖经典RAS信号

Method highlight: Revealing the role of VAV1-like activity
Key finding: Independent of classical RAS signaling
abstract: RHOA, a RAS superfamily member, is frequently mutated in peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL). These mutations are puzzling because variants have opposite effects on conventional RHOA signaling: some (e.g., RHOAG17V) inhibit normal RHOA function, whereas others (e.g., RHOAC16R) are constitutively active. Here we show that all PTCL-associated RHOA mutants acquire a non-canonical VAV1-like activity that activates the transcription factor NFAT. This activity is mediated by complexes between mutant RHOA and the RAP1GDS1607 isoform, is enhanced by T-cell receptor stimulation, and requires components of the T-cell receptor–VAV1 pathway, including PLCγ1 and calcineurin. Unlike canonical RAS superfamily signaling, this neomorphic activity does not require prenylation, the lipid modification anchoring RHOA to membranes. Genetic or pharmacological disruption of this pathway impairs RHOA-mutant PTCL in mouse models and patient-derived cells. These findings explain how mutations with opposing canonical effects converge on a shared oncogenic mechanism and reveal a potential therapeutic vulnerability in RHOA-mutant PTCL. RHOA mutation variants, exerting opposite effects on canonical RHOA signaling, are associated with peripheral T-cell lymphomas (PTCL). Here, the authors show that different RHOA mutants share a neomorphic activity that activates the transcription factor NFAT to drive PTCL.

title: OsCPK17- and OsMPK6-mediated dual phosphorylation of OsPUB12 maintains OsPUB2-regulated OsPUB12 homeostasis and balances rice immunity
summary_zh: OsCPK17和OsMPK6通过磷酸化OsPUB12，维持OsPUB2调控的OsPUB12稳态，平衡水稻免疫。
summary_en: OsCPK17 and OsMPK6 mediate the dual phosphorylation of OsPUB12 to maintain the homeostasis of OsPUB2-regulated OsPUB12 and balance rice immunity.
insights: 创新点：OsCPK17和OsMPK6磷酸化OsPUB12

关键发现：平衡水稻免疫
insights_en: Novelty: OsCPK17 and OsMPK6 phosphorylate OsPUB12
Method highlight: Maintaining OsPUB12 homeostasis

abstract: Numerous E3 ubiquitin ligases regulate plant immunity through mediating protein homeostasis, yet how homeostasis of E3 ligases is finely regulated per se remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal that the ubiquitin E3 ligase plant U-box 2 (OsPUB2) specifically interacts with OsPUB12 and targets it for ubiquitin-mediated degradation. In contrast to the immunity-suppressing role of OsPUB12, OsPUB2 positively regulates resistance to rice bacterial diseases and contributes to pathogen-associated molecular pattern-induced reactive oxygen burst and defense gene expression. Upon pathogen challenge, the calcium-dependent kinase OsCPK17 and mitogen-activated protein kinase OsMPK6 phosphorylate OsPUB12 at Thr154 and Ser460 in a temporally sequential manner. These two phosphorylation events oppositely regulate OsPUB12’s interaction with OsPUB2 and its subsequent ubiquitination, leading to divergent regulation of OsPUB12 stability and rice immunity. Our findings indicate that distinct phosphorylation of OsPUB12 by immune-related kinases OsCPK17 and OsMPK6 synergistically maintains OsPUB2-mediated OsPUB12 homeostasis, serving as a core mechanism to fine-tune rice immunity. OsPUB2 degrades OsPUB12 to promote rice immunity. Phosphorylation of OsPUB12 by OsCPK17 and OsMPK6 at two sites fine-tunes its stability and the plant’s defense response.

summary_en: Studies ISG15 promoting PARP inhibitor resistance in BRCA1-deficient cells by facilitating DNA replication and repair. Finds spontaneous reduction in TP53BP1 expression. Upregulation of ISG15 and ISGylation machinery-related genes.

abstract: Abstract The use of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) has proven largely successful in targeting BRCA1/2 -mutated tumours. However, the emergence of PARPi-resistant disease can reduce the efficacy of this treatment, posing significant challenges in the clinic. Here, we use multiple models of BRCA1 -/- cells and patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) that have been treated with PARPi until they no longer responded to the drug, to characterise genomic and transcriptomic alterations specific to PARPi resistance. We find that abrogation of TP53BP1 expression occurs spontaneously during prolonged PARPi treatment, alongside TP53BP1 genomic deletions and promoter methylation. Additionally, innate immune response genes, including ISG15 and factors of the ISGylation machinery are upregulated in PARPi-resistant cells and tumours. We demonstrate that ISG15 inhibition re-sensitises PARPi-resistant cells to the drug and, conversely, that ISG15 overexpression in BRCA1 -/- cells promotes PARPi resistance. Mechanistically, BRCA1 -/- PARPi-resistant cells rely on ISG15 for replication fork progression and restart of stalled forks and for DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair via homologous recombination (HR). Our results indicate that complex ISG15 interactions with DNA replication/repair factors can drive PARPi resistance in BRCA1-deficient cancer cells and that targeting ISG15 has the potential to overcome PARPi resistance.

title: Izalontamab Brengitecan in Recurrent or Metastatic Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: The PANKU-Esophagus01 Randomized Clinical Trial
summary_zh: 评估izalontamab brengitecan在进展期食管鳞状细胞癌患者中的疗效和安全性。
summary_en: This study evaluates the efficacy and safety of izalontamab brengitecan in patients with advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

New advancements in esophageal cancer treatment
abstract: Importance Effective therapy remains lacking for patients with advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) whose disease progressed after standard treatment. Izalontamab brengitecan, an epidermal growth factor receptor and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate with a topoisomerase I inhibitor, Ed-04, has shown clinical activity in ESCC in a phase 1b study. Objective To evaluate the efficacy and safety of izalontamab brengitecan compared with chemotherapy in patients with advanced ESCC who progressed after first-line programmed cell death 1 protein (PD-1)/programmed cell death 1 ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitor plus platinum-containing chemotherapy. Design, Setting, and Participants This phase 3, open-label, randomized clinical trial was conducted across 80 hospitals in China. Patients with recurrent or metastatic ESCC that had progressed with first-line PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor plus platinum-containing chemotherapy were enrolled. Between March 19, 2024, and August 1, 2025 (final follow-up, October 17, 2025), a total of 704 patients were screened, and 497 were enrolled and randomized. Interventions Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either izalontamab brengitecan (n = 249; 2.5 mg/kg on days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks) or physician-selected chemotherapy (n = 248; irinotecan, paclitaxel, or docetaxel) every 3 weeks. Main Outcomes and Measures The dual primary end points were progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded independent central review according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 and overall survival (OS). Results Of 497 patients who underwent randomization (median age, 61.0 years [range, 34-76]; 448 male patients [90.1%]), 493 received study treatment. At this interim analysis, izalontamab brengitecan demonstrated statistically significant improvement in both PFS and OS. Median PFS by blinded independent central review was 4.17 months (95% CI, 3.61-4.53 months) with izalontamab brengitecan vs 1.97 months (95% CI, 1.61-2.73 months) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.40-0.63; log-rank P < .001). Median OS was 9.79 months (95% CI, 7.89-11.01 months) with izalontamab brengitecan vs 7.20 months (95% CI, 6.18-7.82 months) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.48-0.82; log-rank P < .001). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 212 of 249 patients (85.1%) with izalontamab brengitecan and 147 of 248 patients (59.3%) with chemotherapy and were predominantly hematologic. Conclusions and Relevance Izalontamab brengitecan significantly improved PFS and OS vs chemotherapy in patients with recurrent or metastatic ESCC whose disease had progressed after first-line treatment. These findings support izalontamab brengitecan as a new second-line treatment for this population in China. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06304974

insights: 急性缺血性卒中的症状和诊断

insights_en: Symptoms and diagnosis of acute ischemic stroke
Critical time window for treating acute ischemic stroke
Comparison of different treatment methods
abstract: Importance Acute ischemic stroke, caused by thrombotic or embolic occlusion of a cervical or cerebral artery, leads to neurologic injury due to sudden disruption of blood flow to the brain. Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of disability and death and accounts for about 85% of strokes in the US. Observations Symptoms of acute ischemic stroke vary based on the area of the affected brain. Common presentations include sudden arm or leg weakness, aphasia or slurred speech, sudden loss of balance or coordination, sudden visual difficulties, and/or facial drooping. Patients with suspected stroke should be transported to the nearest emergency department for urgent brain imaging, typically noncontrast computed tomography (CT). Based on 2026 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA) guidelines, first-line therapy for patients with acute ischemic stroke presenting within 4.5 hours from symptom onset with disabling symptoms (eg, affecting the ability to perform activities of daily living) is intravenous thrombolysis (tenecteplase or alteplase) in those without intracranial hemorrhage or other contraindications to thrombolysis. The treatment window can be extended to 9 hours—and up to 24 hours in patients with large vessel occlusion (eg, involving the internal carotid artery or proximal middle cerebral artery [M1 segment]) who are unable to receive thrombectomy—based on identification of salvageable tissue using perfusion imaging with CT perfusion or magnetic resonance imaging. In appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, pooled randomized trial data show an approximately 10% absolute increase in the probability of a better functional outcome with intravenous thrombolysis. Based on 2026 AHA/ASA guidelines, endovascular thrombectomy, which involves clot removal with an intra-arterial mechanical device, is recommended for patients with large vessel occlusion within 6 hours of stroke onset (class 1 recommendation) and is recommended in selected patients with large vessel occlusion within 24 hours of last known well (class 1 recommendation). Endovascular therapy should be performed after intravenous thrombolysis unless patients have contraindications to thrombolytic therapy. Compared with medical management, which includes intravenous thrombolysis when indicated, endovascular thrombectomy produces an approximately 20% absolute increase in functional independence. Conclusions and Relevance Acute ischemic stroke causes substantial disability and mortality. First-line therapy for patients with disabling acute stroke symptoms is intravenous thrombolysis (if no contraindications) within 4.5 hours of stroke onset and up to 24 hours in carefully selected patients not receiving mechanical thrombectomy; for large vessel occlusions, mechanical thrombectomy may be performed up to 24 hours after stroke onset in eligible patients.

abstract: Whether genomic data can be used to effectively predict adaptation in natural populations is unknown. Here, we tested the efficacy of genomic prediction of complex trait evolution by monitoring genome-wide allele frequencies and pigmentation variation in genetically diverse populations of Drosophila melanogaster during evolution in both field mesocosms and a controlled, lab-based setting. At two points during trait evolution, we produced a high-powered, well-resolved genotype-phenotype map that exhibited marked stability across independent populations. Although we were able to use this map to correctly infer the direction of pigmentation evolution in both the lab and field settings, the particular loci responding to selection were largely unpredictable based on the direction of trait evolution itself. Our results hold implications for the promise, and limitations, of genomic prediction.

abstract: Lysosomal Ca 2+ release from acidic stores is critical for lysosomal function, yet the molecular identity of the Ca 2+ uptake conduit has remained elusive. We used a Ca 2+ -imaging–based genetic screen of the lysosomal membrane proteome to identify TMEM184 family proteins as lysosomal Ca 2+ transporters (LyCaTs) essential for Ca 2+ uptake and refilling. TMEM184 selectively transported Ca 2+ while excluding monovalent cations. Loss of TMEM184B/C depleted lysosomal Ca 2+ stores, diminished Ca 2+ release, and disrupted lysosomal exocytosis, biogenesis, and membrane repair, thus phenocopying the release channel transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) deficiency. Moreover, a human TMEM184B mutation associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder compromised lysosomal Ca 2+ transport, and Tmem184b -deficient mice exhibited profound motor impairment. Thus, TMEM184 constitutes the long-sought Ca 2+ uptake and refilling mechanism that governs lysosomal signaling and homeostasis.

abstract: In April 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. ANDV genome sequences were obtained for 10 of the 13 identified cases during a cross-country investigation established to share initial raw data for joint analysis with reciprocal quality control. The genomic data, symptom onsets, and plausible contact patterns strongly support a tightly linked outbreak cluster compatible with a single or very few zoonotic spillover events prior to embarkment followed by human-to-human transmission onboard. The outbreak represents the international displacement of a virus already known to be capable, under specific conditions, to transmit among humans, and does not suggest emergence of a unusual viral strain.

title: Geodetic observations in West Antarctica reveal geodynamically consistent 3D mantle viscosity
summary_zh: 西南极冰盖变化导致地壳运动和重力变化。本研究通过三维地幔粘弹性结构模型，解释了这些变化。

abstract: The rapid ice loss in West Antarctica since the 1990s has led to substantial ice surface lowering, regional bedrock uplift, and gravity reduction, as measured by geodetic observations. The bedrock (crustal) motions and gravity changes result from glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA), a process controlled by Earth’s viscoelastic properties and deglaciation history. In this study, we present GIA models with geodynamically consistent three-dimensional mantle viscoelastic structures and reconstructed ice history for Antarctica from 1900 to 2020, which explain both the observed Global Navigation Satellite System crustal motions and Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment gravity changes in West Antarctica. This study demonstrates that a mantle rheology including a weak asthenosphere and temperature-dependent viscosity is consistent with both mantle convection at million-year timescales and ongoing decadal GIA occurring in West Antarctica.

abstract: Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (T H 1)–like immune architectures in mismatch repair–deficient tumors associated with response to anti–programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair–proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T–dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4 + T cells differentiated into T H 1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding Il7r + early effector CD4 + intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with T H 1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ–dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8 + effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4 + T cell amplification may improve immunotherapy responses.

abstract: The star β Pictoris is orbited by a dusty debris disk, within which planet formation is occurring. The outer disk is sufficiently far from the star that volatile molecules are expected to freeze into solid ices. We observed the β Pictoris disk in the near-infrared using the James Webb Space Telescope. The spectrum shows features due to amorphous water ice (<7% crystallinity) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) ice in both the 12 CO 2 and 13 CO 2 isotopologues. We infer that the CO 2 ice is intimately mixed with the water ice at a ratio of 1:10. This implies that the ices formed in cold conditions, likely in the interstellar medium. Frequent collisions within the debris disk are required to explain the observed uniform distribution of icy dust grains.

abstract: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is the most common preinvasive breast cancer, however our knowledge of the DCIS tumor microenvironment (TME) remains limited. We constructed a comprehensive atlas of the TME in estrogen-receptor positive DCIS using fresh samples collected from normal breast tissues, DCIS and invasive breast cancers. We analyzed 854,911 cells from 159 patients by single cell RNA sequencing and 39 samples by spatial transcriptomics, which identified 9 cell types and 60 cell states. Our data shows remodeling of fibroblasts, vascular and basal cells that encircle the DCIS regions and immunosuppressive ducts that support the growth of the preinvasive cancer cells. This study delineates early alterations in the DCIS TME, including many changes that persist during invasive progression.

abstract: Cilia-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate cell-cell communication and remove signaling molecules from cilia. The Hedgehog receptor Smoothened (SMO) is selected for packaging into ciliary EVs by ubiquitin chains, but how cargo selection is coupled to EV budding remains unknown. In this work, working in mouse kidney cells, we found that the ubiquitin reader endosomal sorting complex required for transport–0 (ESCRT-0) orchestrates both cargo selection and EV biogenesis. Unlike the conventional ESCRT pathway, SMO secretion did not require the ESCRT-III membrane scission machinery. Instead, ESCRT-0 condensed at the ciliary tip, where it clustered ubiquitinated SMO to drive EV biogenesis. Disrupting ESCRT-0 condensation blocked SMO secretion, and combining forced recruitment of ESCRT-0 with optogenetic clustering of SMO was sufficient to reconstitute EV budding. Thus, ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering constitute a minimal module for ESCRT-III–independent reverse-topology budding.

title: A trapped catalytic product acts as molecular glue for innate immune signalosome assembly

abstract: Innate immune systems of living organisms are essential for host defense. Central to these systems is the Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) domain, an evolutionarily conserved module. From antiphage systems in prokaryotes to innate immune systems in plants, TIR domains have catalytic activity. However, TIR domains within animal innate immune receptors, such as Toll-like receptors (TLRs), have been considered as scaffolds for adaptor recruitment. We report that the TLR4 TIR domain possesses an allosterically activated nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) hydrolase (NADase) activity that operates in a single-turnover manner. Its product, adenosine diphosphate ribose, is not released but entrapped as a “molecular glue,” stabilizing a composite catalytic pocket with adaptor TIR domain–containing adaptor protein (TIRAP) to nucleate signalosome assembly. This “produce-and-trap” mechanism represents a signaling mode that integrates enzymatic activity with adaptor function to drive downstream signaling.

abstract: Submarine landslides threaten seabed infrastructure and trigger the transport of globally important amounts of sediment, carbon, and pollutants to deep-sea environments. However, fully submarine landslides have never been directly monitored in nature. Past hypotheses for their failure mechanism and dynamics therefore remain unvalidated for natural settings, including that prolonged upslope-migrating failures (breaching) occur in sandy seafloor environments. In this work, we present direct underwater monitoring of fully submarine landslides at Homathko Delta in western Canada that retrogress slowly upslope, indicating breaching-type failure. Their prolonged rather than instantaneous nature has important implications for the stress that seabed structures must be designed to withstand. Prolonged landslides also initiate sustained sediment flows (turbidity currents) that efficiently transport sediment, carbon, and pollutants further offshore.

abstract: In 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. Analyses revealed an unexpected relationship to an outbreak in Argentina in 2018. Retrospective investigation clarified the 2018 outbreak could involve person-to-person transmission and a common ANDV lineage spanned HPS cases from 2018 to 2025 in a geographically defined area in northern Patagonia, without widespread community transmission of ANDV. Route reconstruction for the index cases in the cruise ship outbreak identified geographically plausible exposures to viruses of this lineage in Argentina, but their timing was inconsistent with the expected ANDV incubation period. The infection source for the cruise ship outbreak cannot be resolved with current information, highlighting the need to expand viral surveillance in the ANDV endemic region.

abstract: The Earth is warming, but not all regions are warming equally. In high mountain areas, temperatures are generally increasing by 1.5 to 2 times the global average, sometimes with devastating consequences. A small or gradual change in the mountain cryosphere—perhaps progressive thawing of frozen ground or a flood from a small glacial lake—can suddenly turn into a cascade of catastrophes with enormous ramifications. Monitoring systems for the cryosphere in high mountain areas have traditionally been designed to look at individual components and changes. What are the temperature and depth of the permafrost, or how much area is covered by snow, and what is the related avalanche danger? Many of the monitoring and warning systems were designed for historical patterns of snowfall or rainfall, and a river gauge may no longer be adequate if there is greater flow in the rainy season, or increased sediment that could damage the gauge.

abstract: The cryosphere plays a vital role in regulating planetary dynamics and habitability, yet it remains unclear whether its essential functions remain within a safe operating space (SOS) amid Anthropocene change. Here, we propose a cryosphere SOS and systematically evaluate its contributions to Earth system resilience using the planetary boundaries framework. Multiple lines of evidence indicate an accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity, driven by amplifying feedbacks. Key cryospheric control variables either have left or are committed to departing from Holocene-like conditions. We conclude that the cryosphere has breached its SOS and is on a trajectory that locks in long-term risks for human societies and ecosystems. Safeguarding planetary resilience therefore requires explicit consideration of cryosphere change and its interactions across the Earth system.

abstract: In this paper we analyze the hierarchical topological cascade of knotted and linked filaments associated with the natural decay of superfluid vortex tangles. This is done by using an algebraic reformulation of knot polynomial invariants to quantify the topological states of the cascade process. By interpreting the evolutionary paths associated with vortex knot dynamics as geodesic flows in an appropriate knot polynomial space defined by adapted Jones polynomials [X. Liu, R. L. Ricca, J. Phys. A Math. Theor. 45 , 205501 (2012).], we introduce an entanglement index to quantify the probability density of occurrence of each topological state. By this method we analyze all prime knots, links, and composites up to 8 crossings, and show that this measure detects accurately the decreasing topological complexity observed in simulations and laboratory experiments. By a comparative analysis carried out with data based on an alternative measure (complexity degree), we show that this entanglement index proves to be a more robust and reliable quantifier. The theoretical framework proposed here can be applied to other types of physical systems, where networks of filamentary structures are subject to continuous topological change and reorganization.

summary_zh: 研究卵巢癌化疗耐药性，开发nFANet分析核F-actin。发现铂类化疗诱导核F-actin组装，p38α-MAPK-MK2轴调控其动态聚合。

Method highlight: Combines nFANet with kinase screen
Key finding: p38α-MAPK-MK2 axis regulates nuclear F-actin assembly
abstract: Nuclear F-actin facilitates DNA damage repair and contributes to cancer chemoresistance. However, the regulatory mechanisms controlling its dynamic polymerization in response to genotoxic stress remain poorly defined. A major barrier in nuclear actin research is the lack of tools for precise, high-throughput analysis. To systematically investigate nuclear F-actin assembly in DNA damage response, we developed a deep learning pipeline, named nFANet, for high-throughput detection and analysis of nuclear F-actin. Here, using ovarian cancer—a malignancy where chemoresistance is a major clinical obstacle—as a model, we showed that platinum-based chemotherapy robustly induces nuclear F-actin assembly. A subsequent kinome screening, in combination with the application of nFANet, identified the kinase p38α MAPK as a critical upstream regulator of platinum-induced nuclear F-actin assembly. Mechanistically, the p38α MAPK–MK2 signaling pathway promotes formin-mediated nuclear F-actin assembly in response to chemotherapy. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition or genetic knockout of the p38α MAPK–MK2 pathway sensitized ovarian cancer cells to platinum-based therapy. Our work uncovers a key mechanism governing nuclear actin remodeling under genotoxic stress and lays the foundation for identifying a patient subgroup likely to benefit from therapeutic targeting of this pathway.

summary_zh: 研究mGlu2受体与Gq、Gi蛋白协同作用，发现Gi/o-coupled mGlu2受体可产生钙信号，独立于Gq-coupled受体二聚化。
summary_en: Studies the synergistic effect of mGlu2 receptors with Gq and Gi proteins, finds that Gi/o-coupled mGlu2 receptors can generate calcium signals independently of dimerization of Gq-coupled receptors.
