Method highlight: Studies the function of mGlu2 receptors in neurons
Key finding: Gi/o-coupled mGlu2 receptors generate calcium signals independently of dimerization of Gq-coupled receptors
abstract: The capacity of one G protein–coupled receptor (GPCR) to modulate signaling outputs of another is a phenomenon with potential implications for neuron function and therapeutic action. Notably, Gi/o-coupled receptors have been shown to generate calcium signals after costimulation of Gq-coupled receptors, an effect resulting from a crosstalk between signaling cascades. But the relevance for brain function and for therapeutic applications remains largely unclear. Here we show that Gi/o-coupled metabotropic glutamate 2 (mGlu2) receptors can generate calcium signals in neurons. It results from either agonist activation or constitutive activity of a Gq-coupled receptor endogenously coexpressed with mGlu2, independently of dimerization. Specifically, the constitutively active platelet-activating factor receptor (PAFR) plays an essential role in mGlu2-calcium signaling in hippocampal neurons, an effect largely inhibited by PAFR inverse agonists and genetic variants. This mGlu2-PAFR crosstalk is required for the cognitive and behavioral rescue produced by mGlu2 agonists in a mouse model of NMDA receptor hypofunction. These data highlight the complexity of GPCR signaling and provide key insights on therapeutic strategies for psychiatric disorders.

title: Diffusional depth profiling using electrochemiluminescence microscopy
summary_zh: 研究电化学发光显微镜扩散深度分析，发现增加发光体浓度可获取3D信息，通过调节浓度比控制发射层扩散。
summary_en: Studies diffusional depth profiling with electrochemiluminescence microscopy, finds that increasing luminophore concentration enables access to 3D information, and controlling emission layer diffusion by tuning concentration ratio.
insights: 创新点：提出电化学发光显微镜扩散深度分析新方法
方法亮点：通过调节浓度比控制发射层扩散
关键发现：增加发光体浓度获取3D信息
insights_en: Novelty: Proposes a new method for diffusional depth profiling with electrochemiluminescence microscopy
Method highlight: Controls emission layer diffusion by tuning concentration ratio
Key finding: Gaining 3D information by increasing luminophore concentration
abstract: Electrochemiluminescence (ECL) microscopy has emerged as a powerful 2D imaging technique with exceptional spatial resolution, enabling visualization of biological entities, nanomaterials, and multiphase systems. Conventional ECL experiments rely on coreactant concentrations in large excess of the luminophore to generate a bright signal in the vicinity of the electrode. While effective for surface interrogation, this confinement limits resolution in the z-dimension, making 3D imaging challenging. Here, we show that introducing an excess of luminophore enables access to 3D information through diffusion of the emission layer away from the electrode. By tuning the concentration ratio of tris(2,2’-bipyridine)ruthenium(II) ([Ru(bpy) 3 ] 2+ ) to tri-n-propylamine (TPrA), we control emission layer diffusivity. Initially, ECL arises from heterogeneous oxidation of both species at the electrode. As TPrA is depleted, the mechanism shifts to chemiluminescence, where [Ru(bpy) 3 ] 3+ oxidizes TPrA, generating a diffusing emissive layer that extends in the z-direction over time. Simulations and scanning electrochemical microscopy capture these diffusion profiles and highlight the role of concentration ratios. We apply this “diffusional depth profiling” to spirulina algae and spheroid cell models, insulating bodies that block light coming from the evolving emissive layer, revealing 3D morphology. This work uncovers the important influence of time and concentration on ECL emission layer expansion for depth profiling micro-to-mesoscale entities across biology and materials science.

title: Does Foveal Morphology Influence Postoperative Refractive Prediction Error Following Cataract Surgery?
summary_zh: 研究白内障手术后黄斑形态与屈光预测误差的关系，发现术前黄斑形态与术后屈光预测误差相关。
summary_en: Studies the relationship between foveal morphology and postoperative refractive prediction error after cataract surgery, finds that preoperative foveal morphology is associated with postoperative refractive prediction error.
insights: 创新点：评估白内障手术后黄斑形态与屈光预测误差的关系
方法亮点：使用光学相干断层扫描评估黄斑形态
关键发现：术前黄斑形态与术后屈光预测误差相关
insights_en: Novelty: Evaluates the relationship between foveal morphology and postoperative refractive prediction error after cataract surgery
Method highlight: Uses optical coherence tomography to assess foveal morphology
Key finding: Preoperative foveal morphology is associated with postoperative refractive prediction error
abstract: Background: In this study, we evaluated whether preoperative foveal morphology assessed using optical coherence tomography is associated with postoperative absolute refractive prediction error after uncomplicated cataract surgery. Methods: This retrospective observational study screened 435 patients and included 91 eyes of 91 patients after exclusions. All included patients underwent phacoemulsification with monofocal intraocular lens implantation. Preoperative spectral-domain optical coherence tomography measurements were used to calculate a foveal steepness index (FSI) as the ratio of the mean inner Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) ring thickness to minimum foveal thickness, and foveal depth as the difference between these measurements. The primary outcome was SRK/T-derived absolute prediction error (APE) at one month. A supplementary analysis used Barrett Universal II. Associations were examined using Spearman correlation and univariable and multivariable linear regression analyses. A sensitivity analysis was performed after zeroing the cohort mean signed prediction error. Results: The mean age was 68.2 ± 7.8 years. The mean absolute prediction error was 0.48 ± 0.37 D, with a median of 0.50 D (IQR, 0.25–0.75 D). Overall, 70.3% and 95.6% of eyes had errors within 0.50 and 1.00 D, respectively. FSI and foveal depth were significantly associated with APE in univariable analyses (p = 0.028 and p = 0.013, respectively). The adjusted foveal-depth association was not statistically significant in the primary analysis (p = 0.079) but reached significance after zeroing the mean prediction error (p = 0.032). The supplementary Barrett Universal II analysis did not confirm an adjusted association before or after zeroing the mean signed prediction error. Adding foveal depth did not meaningfully improve leave-one-out cross-validated performance. Conclusions: These exploratory findings suggest a possible association between foveal morphology and SRK/T-derived APE in this study population. Reproducibility across IOL calculation formulas and clinical applicability remain uncertain; validation in a larger prospective cohort is needed.

title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss
summary_zh: 研究显示，TDP-43缺失导致神经元结构完整但突触通信严重受损。通过基因校正UNC13A的隐式剪接事件，可以恢复突触功能。开发了一种纠正人类神经元和人类化小鼠模型中UNC13A隐式剪接的寡核苷酸。
summary_en: The study shows that TDP-43 depletion leads to a predegenerative state with intact neurons but substantial breakdown in synaptic communication. Genetic correction of a single cryptic splicing event in UNC13A can rescue these deficits. A splice-switching antisense oligonucleotide was developed to correct UNC13A cryptic splicing in human neurons and a humanized mouse model.
insights: 创新点：发现TDP-43缺失影响突触功能
方法亮点：基因校正UNC13A隐式剪接
关键发现：恢复突触功能
insights_en: Novelty: TDP-43 depletion affects synaptic function
Method highlight: Genetic correction of UNC13A cryptic splicing
Key finding: Rescue of synaptic function
abstract: Abstract TDP-43 nuclear depletion is a defining pathological feature of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia that induces widespread cryptic splicing defects in hundreds of transcripts 1–8 . Despite this, whether TDP-43 loss affects synaptic function has remained unclear. Here we show that TDP-43 loss induces a predegenerative state in which neurons remain structurally intact but suffer a substantial breakdown in synaptic communication. Genetic correction of a single cryptic splicing event in UNC13A was sufficient to rescue these deficits. We developed splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides that correct UNC13A cryptic splicing in human cortical and spinal motor neurons and in a humanized mouse model. In human neurons this intervention restored spontaneous and evoked synaptic vesicle release, release probability at individual synapses and wider network synchrony. Together, this establishes UNC13A splice correction as a mechanistically defined and genetically validated therapeutic strategy relevant to roughly 97% of patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and roughly 50% of patients with frontotemporal dementia with TDP-43 pathology.

title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis
summary_zh: 研究发现，中性粒细胞和巨噬细胞分泌的IL-1β稳定低UCP1表达的BA-L细胞。IL-1β确保H6PD蛋白降解，生成活性糖皮质激素，激活GR，增加Rgs2表达，从而抑制UCP1表达。
summary_en: The study finds that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes BA-L cells with low UCP1 expression. IL-1β ensures the degradation of H6PD protein, generating active glucocorticoids, activating the GR, and increasing Rgs2 expression, thereby suppressing UCP1 expression.
insights: 创新点：发现IL-1β稳定BA-L细胞
方法亮点：研究IL-1β对UCP1表达的影响
关键发现：抑制UCP1表达
insights_en: Novelty: IL-1β stabilizes BA-L cells
Method highlight: Study the effect of IL-1β on UCP1 expression
Key finding: Inhibition of UCP1 expression
abstract: Abstract Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity 1–5 . We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells) 6 . Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by Nr3c1 ) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 ( Rgs2 ), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of Nr3c1 during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal–immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals.

title: Co-administration of the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 and bivalent Ancestral/BA.1 vaccination is well-tolerated in immunosuppressed patients highly vulnerable to infection with SARS-CoV-2 virus: the results of the multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled, RAPID-PROTECTION trial
summary_zh: 研究AZD7442抗体与mRNA疫苗联合使用的安全性。结果显示，联合使用耐受性良好，抗体水平升高。
summary_en: This study investigates the safety of co-administering the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 with a bivalent mRNA vaccine. The results show that the combination is well-tolerated, with increased antibody levels.
insights: 创新点：联合使用抗体和疫苗提高免疫效果
方法亮点：多中心随机对照试验
关键发现：联合使用安全有效
insights_en: Novelty: Co-administration of antibody and vaccine to enhance immunogenicity
Method highlight: Multicentre randomised controlled trial
Key finding: Combination is safe and effective
abstract: Abstract Immunocompromised individuals remain at risk of severe COVID-19. This multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled trial evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics and immunogenicity of co-administering the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 with a bivalent (Ancestral/BA.1) mRNA/LNP SARS-CoV-2 vaccine. A total of 139 immunocompromised adults received AZD7442 followed 28 days later by vaccination. AZD7442 was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events. Serum AZD7442 concentrations peaked at day 28 and remained detectable across disease cohorts at day 180. Anti-Spike antibody responses increased after AZD7442 and reached their highest levels after vaccination. Although binding antibodies against Omicron variants increased post-vaccination, neutralisation of Omicron remained limited after both AZD7442 and vaccination. Vaccination preferentially boosted antibodies targeting S2, the S1 N-terminal domain and receptor-binding domain epitopes not bound by AZD7442, and increased S2-specific memory B cells. Vaccine-induced T-cell responses were cross-reactive between ancestral and Omicron variants. Our findings support consideration of combined antibody and vaccine strategies in future therapeutic antibody development. The trial is registered with the International Standard Randomised Controlled Trial Number registry (ISRCTN53507177).

title: AS01E-adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial
authors: On behalf of the RSV OA=ADJ-023 Study Group
summary_zh: 研究AS01E佐剂RSV疫苗在移植患者中的免疫原性和安全性。结果显示，疫苗安全有效。
summary_en: This study investigates the immunogenicity and safety of the AS01E-adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplants. The results show that the vaccine is safe and effective.
insights: 创新点：研究移植患者疫苗接种效果
方法亮点：随机对照试验
关键发现：疫苗安全有效
insights_en: Novelty: Investigating vaccine efficacy in transplant patients
Method highlight: Randomised controlled trial
Key finding: Vaccine is safe and effective
abstract: Abstract Immunocompromised adults are at increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease. This multicountry, open-label phase 2b trial (NCT05921903) evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the AS01 E -adjuvanted RSV prefusion F protein vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) over 12 months in kidney or lung transplant recipients ≥18 years, randomized 1:1 to receive one ( n = 131) or two doses 30–60 days apart ( n = 130). A control group of non-immunocompromised adults ≥50 years ( n = 125) received a single dose. The primary outcome was the mean geometric increase in RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing titers one month following a second adjuvanted RSVPreF3 dose relative to the first dose in transplant recipients. Secondary outcomes included assessment of the safety and immunogenicity of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in transplant recipients compared with the control group. In transplant recipients receiving two doses, neutralizing titers against RSV-A and RSV-B were numerically higher one month post-dose 2 than post-dose 1 (mean geometric increases: 1.34 [95% CI: 1.20, 1.48] for RSV-A [ n = 111] and 1.26 [95% CI: 1.14, 1.40] for RSV-B [ n = 111]). A single dose was immunogenic in transplant recipients, but showed slower and generally lower initial neutralizing responses than in non-immunocompromised controls, specifically in individuals receiving mycophenolate. RSVPreF3-specific CD4 + T-cell frequencies increased after vaccination versus baseline in all groups. Humoral and cell-mediated immune responses remained above baseline for 12 months post-vaccination. Both doses of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and had a similar and acceptable safety profile. Overall, these results support a favorable benefit-risk profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in kidney and lung transplant recipients.

title: A microfluidic fluorescence lifetime screening platform bridges in vitro and in vivo formats and enables discovery of Amyloid β aggregation inhibitors
summary_zh: 开发了一种微流控荧光寿命筛选平台。用于体外和体内筛选β-淀粉样蛋白聚集抑制剂。发现新的抑制剂。
summary_en: Developed a microfluidic fluorescence lifetime screening platform. Used for in vitro and in vivo screening of Amyloid β aggregation inhibitors. Identified new inhibitors.
insights: 微流控平台提高筛选效率
荧光寿命技术用于筛选抑制剂
发现新的β-淀粉样蛋白抑制剂
insights_en: Microfluidic platform enhances screening efficiency
Fluorescence lifetime technique for inhibitor screening
Identification of new Amyloid β aggregation inhibitors
abstract: Abstract Inhibiting the aggregation of Amyloid β (1-42) is a promising strategy for the development of disease-modifying Alzheimer’s disease therapeutics. To date, however, no sufficiently efficacious inhibitors have been identified, despite the best efforts of more than 200 advanced drug development campaigns. This failure can be partially attributed to limitations in current in vitro compound screening and in vivo validation assays. Here, we report a high throughput assay platform based on the use of a fluorescence lifetime aggregation sensor that can be applied in vitro and in vivo. This microfluidic “nanoFLIM” assay presents a cost-effective and reliable alternative to conventional early-stage small molecule discovery platforms for cell-free Amyloid β aggregation. The fluorescence lifetime sensor can dynamically monitor peptide aggregation in cellular and Caenorhabditis elegans disease models, providing directly comparable aggregation kinetics, which is not achievable by any other method. The power of this unified platform for accelerating hit-to-lead strategies, lowering attrition rates and expediting in vivo screening, was demonstrated with a pilot screening campaign of 445 compounds, revealing an inhibitor that can inhibit Amyloid β self-assembly both in vitro as well as in cellular and whole organism disease models.

title: Analyzing epigenetic modifications at sample-specific CpG loci in long-read data using a likelihood-based framework in bsseq
summary_zh: 提出一种基于似然框架的bsseq方法。用于分析长读长数据中的样本特异CpG位点。提高分析精度。
summary_en: Proposed a likelihood-based framework in bsseq for analyzing sample-specific CpG loci in long-read data. Enhances analysis accuracy.
insights: bsseq方法分析CpG位点
提高CpG位点识别精度
样本特异CpG位点分析
insights_en: bsseq method for analyzing CpG loci
Enhanced precision in CpG locus identification
Analysis of sample-specific CpG loci
abstract: SUMMARY: DNA in CpG context is often epigenetically modified in vertebrate genomes which increases their mutation rate. However, it remains challenging to identify sample-specific CpG loci for analysis of epigenetic modifications. Here, we present a read-based likelihood framework for identifying reference and non-reference CpG loci with high precision and sensitivity in single-molecule long-read sequencing data from Nanopore and PacBio platforms. Including all sample-specific CpG loci increases the number of analyzable loci and reduces bias in modification level estimates, both critical factors for accurate analyses of epigenetic modifications. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The likelihood framework is implemented in the R package bsseq with the source code available on github https://github.com/hansenlab/bsseq. Installation instructions and a user guide for long-read analysis and likelihood-based filtering of CpG loci are available on Bioconductor https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/bsseq.html. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: A systematic review of EC number prediction algorithms based on reaction chemical structures
summary_zh: 系统综述基于反应化学结构的EC编号预测算法。分类方法并讨论其优缺点。
summary_en: Systematic review of EC number prediction algorithms based on reaction chemical structures. Classifies methods and discusses their advantages and disadvantages.
insights: EC编号预测算法综述
反应化学结构方法分类
算法优缺点分析
insights_en: Review of EC number prediction algorithms
Classification of reaction chemical structure methods
Analysis of algorithm advantages and disadvantages
abstract: MOTIVATION: Enzymes catalyse most of the metabolic reactions in living organisms. The functional characterization of enzymes is critical to understand the metabolic processes involved in different fields such as biotechnology, nutrition, ecology, and drug development. The Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers provide a hierarchical framework for classifying enzymatic reactions, linking gene and protein sequences to biochemical transformations. However, the incomplete annotation of biochemical reaction databases limits the accurate representation of metabolism of living organisms. RESULTS: To address this gap, several computational methods have been developed to predict EC numbers from reaction chemical structures, broadly classified into reaction similarity-based and machine/deep learning approaches. We systematically review these tools, comparing their performance predicting EC numbers from different databases, and assessing their robustness across enzyme classes. We also apply these methods to predict EC numbers from drug metabolism reactions, highlighting their potential to improve functional annotation of uncharacterized metabolic pathways. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: All the necessary data and code to reproduce the results of this manuscript are available within https://github.com/PlanesLab/ECNumberPrediction GitHub repository and in Zenodo https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22957403. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: ROOF: Robustness-Oriented Optimal Factorization for Fluorescence Crosstalk Correction
summary_zh: 提出ROOF方法，用于荧光串扰校正。结合校准建模和数据驱动光谱解混。
summary_en: Proposes the ROOF method for fluorescence crosstalk correction. Combines calibration-based modeling with data-driven spectral unmixing.
insights: ROOF方法校正荧光串扰
结合校准和数据驱动方法
提高校正鲁棒性
insights_en: ROOF method for crosstalk correction
Combination of calibration and data-driven approaches
Improved robustness of correction
abstract: MOTIVATION: Fluorescence bleed-through (spectral crosstalk) compromises the accuracy of signal interpretation, quantification, and visualization in multi-band fluorescence microscopy. Existing correction methods rely either on experimental calibration or blind spectral unmixing, but often suffer from limited robustness to biological variability, overcorrection artifacts, or the need for manual parameter tuning. We propose ROOF (Robustness-Oriented Optimal Factorization), a semi-blind framework that unifies calibration-based modeling with data-driven spectral unmixing. It formulates crosstalk correction as a diagonally normalized nonnegative matrix factorization problem regularized by a reference crosstalk matrix obtained from single-labeled control samples. The regularization parameter is estimated automatically via maximum likelihood, eliminating manual tuning while adapting to specimen-specific variations. RESULTS: Experiments on synthetic and real four-band fluorescence images demonstrate that ROOF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art crosstalk correction methods. ROOF achieves higher correction accuracy, suppresses overcorrection artifacts, preserves biologically meaningful fluorescence colocalization, and is computationally efficient. These results highlight ROOF's robustness, efficiency, and practical value for reliable quantitative fluorescence imaging. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The codes are available at https://github.com/baobabking/ROOF with DOI:10.5281/zenodo.21872937.

title: Leveraging amino acid embeddings for accurate translation efficiency prediction
summary_zh: 利用氨基酸嵌入进行翻译效率预测。提高预测准确性。
summary_en: Utilizes amino acid embeddings for accurate translation efficiency prediction. Enhances prediction accuracy.
insights: 氨基酸嵌入提高预测准确性
结合氨基酸信息预测翻译效率
翻译效率预测新方法
insights_en: Amino acid embeddings improve prediction accuracy
Combining amino acid information for translation efficiency prediction
Novel approach for translation efficiency prediction
abstract: MOTIVATION: Accurate prediction of translation efficiency from mRNA sequences is an important step toward mRNA sequence design. In recent years, the widespread adoption of high-resolution ribosome profiling techniques, such as Ribo-seq, has led to rapid accumulation of large-scale datasets that capture the relationship between mRNA sequences and translation efficiency. This progress has facilitated the development of machine-learning-based models for translation efficiency prediction. However, most existing approaches rely primarily on mRNA-derived features, such as codon usage frequency and 5' untranslated regions (5'UTRs), and do not directly utilize the amino-acid-level information. RESULTS: In this study, we show that incorporating distributed representations (embeddings) of amino acid sequences translated from mRNA as model features can improve translation efficiency prediction. By combining fixed amino acid embeddings derived from a pretrained protein language model with mRNA-derived features, the proposed model integrates complementary protein-level and nucleotide-level information for more accurate prediction of translation efficiency. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: Codes are available at GitHub (https://github.com/gterai/AA_emb) and Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23968476).

title: Integer quantized multilayer perceptron neural network for lossless compression of nanopore signal
summary_zh: 提出整数量化多层感知器神经网络。用于无损压缩纳米孔信号。
summary_en: Proposes an integer quantized multilayer perceptron neural network for lossless compression of nanopore signals.
insights: 整数量化神经网络压缩信号
提高纳米孔信号压缩性能
学习模型压缩纳米孔信号
insights_en: Integer quantized neural network for signal compression
Improved compression performance of nanopore signals
Learning-based model for nanopore signal compression
abstract: MOTIVATION: Nanopore sequencing is indispensable for advanced genomic analyses, but the raw signal output creates substantial storage and bandwidth demands. Specialized model-free compressors such as VBZ and ex-zd have been proposed to address this challenge. They deliver high throughput and strong compression performance, yet they cannot fully exploit higher-order statistical dependencies, which limits further gains. Learning-based compressors can achieve better compression ratios, but they often introduce floating-point non-determinism and are too slow for large-scale nanopore datasets, reducing their practicality. RESULTS: We introduce SigComp, a learned lossless compressor for nanopore signal data. SigComp employs a compact multilayer perceptron network with a fixed context window to capture higher-order dependencies within the dominant one-byte signal deltas. By integrating post-training quantization and a fully GPU-native range coder, SigComp eliminates GPU-CPU synchronization overhead in the autoregressive coding loop while ensuring strict bit-exactness across diverse execution settings. Evaluations on diverse species and sequencing chemistries (DNA R10.4.1 and RNA004) demonstrate that SigComp consistently reduces compressed file sizes by 6.00%-7.09% and 3.86%-5.34% over VBZ and ex-zd, respectively, albeit with a 10× lower processing throughput. Compared to the leading neural compressor, SigComp achieves a comparable compression ratio, sacrificing merely 0.4%-1.9%, while delivering 46-74× higher throughput. Ablation studies confirm that SigComp's integer-only, GPU-native approach improves throughput by 7.75-8.30× overall over hybrid GPU-CPU pipelines without model quantization, and the default 64-symbol context window effectively captures the vast majority of exploitable redundancy. SigComp can also be extended to lossy compression by eliminating the least significant bits, and achieve compression ratios of 4.047-4.868, outperforming lossy ex-zd by 9.18%-14.38%. Although processing remains slower than specialized codecs, SigComp offers an excellent trade-off for long-term cold archival storage, particularly when scaled via multi-GPU environments. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: SigComp is freely available on GitHub at: https://github.com/BioinfoSZU/SigComp. It supports CPU-only, NVIDIA, and AMD GPU execution backends with seamless cross-platform archive interoperability, as well as multi-GPU scaling. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

People know who to ask for favors despite underestimating compliance
summary_zh: 研究揭示人们虽低估他人同意度，但能准确判断求助对象。通过分析求助行为，发现人际感知存在多样性。
summary_en: The study reveals that people can accurately judge who to ask for favors despite underestimating compliance. Analyzing favor-asking behavior, it finds diverse interpersonal perception.
insights: 创新点：人际感知多样性

关键发现：低估他人同意度但准确判断求助对象

Method highlight: Analyzing favor-asking behavior
Key finding: Underestimating compliance but accurately judging who to ask for favors
abstract: Whether and how people approach social interactions hinges on how they expect others to respond. Extensive social psychology research suggests that people are inaccurate interpersonal perceivers, overestimating negative responses (e.g., discomfort) and underestimating positive responses (e.g., appreciation) across a variety of social situations. However, this conclusion is based almost exclusively on mean-level bias analyses that obscure the dyadic nature of interpersonal judgment and rely on a narrow conceptualization of interpersonal accuracy. Leveraging research on favor-asking and anticipated compliance as an exemplar, we demonstrate that interpersonal accuracy takes multiple theoretically distinct forms, and that the prevailing conclusion that people misunderstand their influence over others—because they tend to underestimate compliance—is likely overgeneralized. Across four studies (13,196 directed dyadic ratings), we show that people accurately differentiate between who will comply with their favor requests (dyadic meta-accuracy) despite the average tendency to underestimate compliance (mean-level bias). This pattern emerged for specific and general favor requests, among well- and newly-acquainted individuals, and beyond what could be expected due to self-projection. Through this dyadic lens, people are highly adept judges of their influence over others, as they are able to target their requests toward individuals who are uniquely likely to acquiesce to them—and can avoid wasting time on those who are not. Thus, our research refines existing implications for how people approach asking for favors. More broadly, by aligning theory, measurement, and level of analysis, our studies elucidate the need for greater theoretical precision and empirical breadth in interpersonal accuracy research.

Method highlight: Randomized controlled trial design
Key finding: Intervention effectively reduces cases of influenza-like illness
abstract: Public health recommendations often advise people to isolate when infected with influenza-like illness (ILI) with the goal of promoting physical distancing and limiting face-to-face interactions when risk of transmission is highest. Because isolation may have negative consequences, it is important to carefully assess whether encouragement to physically distance actually prevents cases of ILI. College campuses can be especially vulnerable to outbreaks of ILI and are ideal environments for assessing the impact of encouragement-to-physically-distance interventions. The eX-FLU cluster-randomized trial followed 579 students on a college campus over a ten-week period during flu season to evaluate such an intervention. Students in the trial were randomized to receive the intervention—encouragement to isolate in their dorm room when symptomatic for ILI—or control. Evaluating the effect of this intervention is challenging because of dependence between students in the trial and an anticipated spillover effect of the intervention. Moreover, while the intervention was designed to affect both face-to-face interactions and ILI infections, the effect on ILI infections is of primary public health interest. In this paper, a randomization-based testing procedure is proposed to assess the intervention effect specifically on ILI infections in the presence of dependent data and spillover effects. The testing procedure is shown theoretically and empirically to control the type I error rate and have good statistical power to detect an intervention effect in trials similar to eX-FLU. When applied to the eX-FLU data, this testing procedure gives moderate evidence that the intervention reduced ILI infections.

title: Selectively disrupting lysine acetyltransferase p300 and ZEB1 interaction prevents tumor progression while enhancing antitumor immunity
summary_zh: 研究提出选择性破坏p300和ZEB1相互作用可抑制肿瘤进展并增强抗肿瘤免疫。发现p300与ZEB1相互作用促进肿瘤细胞生长。
summary_en: The study proposes that selectively disrupting the interaction between lysine acetyltransferase p300 and ZEB1 prevents tumor progression while enhancing antitumor immunity. It finds that the interaction promotes tumor cell growth.
insights: 创新点：选择性破坏p300和ZEB1相互作用
方法亮点：研究肿瘤细胞生长机制
关键发现：p300与ZEB1相互作用促进肿瘤细胞生长
insights_en: Novelty: Selectively disrupting the interaction between p300 and ZEB1
Method highlight: Studying tumor cell growth mechanisms
Key finding: p300 and ZEB1 interaction promotes tumor cell growth
abstract: Both p300 acetyltransferase inhibitors and bromodomain inhibitors show therapeutic promise in cancer, but they mostly exhibit limited efficacy and may elicit severe adverse effects due to their lack of targeting selectivity. Thus, selectively disrupting p300 interactions with specific pro-oncogenic targets that are specifically expressed in neoplastic cells could serve as a safe and effective strategy for cancer treatment. Here, we demonstrate that p300 interacts with the pro-oncogenic transcription factor, ZEB1, and catalyzes its acetylation at an evolutionarily conserved K80 residue, stabilizing its expression in aggressive cancer cells. Ectopic expression of wild-type ZEB1 (mostly in acetylated status) but not the acetylation-deficient ZEB1 mutant modulates cytokinome of cancer cells, creating an immune-suppressive tumor microenvironment to support cancer progression. Underlining the importance of ZEB1 posttranslational processing, the K80-acetylated transcription factor is highly expressed in human cancers where its high-level expression is associated with poor prognosis. Importantly, we identify a small molecule compound, WY6, that undergoes high-affinity binding to p300 TAZ2 domain (a domain critical for ZEB1 binding) and consequently disrupts ZEB1 binding to p300, thereby suppressing K80 acetylation. WY6 treatment of tumor cells effectively represses p300-mediated ZEB1 acetylation, promoting its ubiquitination and subsequent degradation. Moreover, in vivo, WY6 potently suppresses orthotopic tumor growth without eliciting obvious toxic side effects and exhibits a synergetic effect when combined with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade immunotherapy. Collectively, our data demonstrate that selective disrupting of p300 and ZEB1 interaction effectively prevents tumor progression and may offer a promising therapeutic strategy for p300–ZEB1 axis-driven malignancies.

title: Reply to Neogi: Reaffirming the ~3.5 Ga age of the Bhitar Dari carbonaceous chert
ChREBP drives diabetic kidney disease, and its inhibition confers renal protection
summary_zh: 研究发现ChREBP驱动糖尿病肾病，其抑制可提供肾脏保护。通过转录组筛选发现ChREBP在糖尿病肾脏中显著上调。
summary_en: The study finds that ChREBP drives diabetic kidney disease, and its inhibition provides renal protection. Transcriptome screening reveals significantly up-regulated ChREBP in diabetic kidneys.
insights: 创新点：发现ChREBP驱动糖尿病肾病
方法亮点：转录组筛选技术
关键发现：ChREBP抑制提供肾脏保护
insights_en: Novelty: Identified ChREBP as a driver of diabetic kidney disease
Method highlight: Transcriptome screening techniques
Key finding: ChREBP inhibition provides renal protection
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) represents a major medical burden. Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a leading cause of CKD, but intracellular pathways that can be pharmacologically targeted are poorly defined. Using transcriptome screening of DKD model mice we found that a carbohydrate-responsive element–binding protein (ChREBP)-dependent transcriptional cascade is markedly up-regulated in diabetic kidneys. Genetic ablation of ChREBP in diabetic mice ameliorated DKD, establishing ChREBP as a potential causal driver. A chemical screen based on ChREBP transcriptional activity identified D-532 as a small-molecule inhibitor that is effective in human and rodent cells. Oral administration of D-532 protected multiple diabetic mouse models from DKD progression and suppressed ChREBP and its downstream targets, including genes associated with excessive reactive oxygen species production. These findings position ChREBP as a pharmacologically targetable transcriptional driver of DKD and provide proof of concept that ChREBP inhibition can confer renal protection.

title: Two-phase NEUROD1 pioneer activity synchronizes sensory neuronal differentiation and subtype specification
summary_zh: 研究揭示NEUROD1在神经分化中的双阶段调控作用。通过基因敲除和转录组分析，发现NEUROD1调控神经元分化时间。
summary_en: The study reveals the two-phase pioneer activity of NEUROD1 in neuronal differentiation. Through gene knockout and transcriptomic analysis, it finds that NEUROD1 regulates the timing of neuronal differentiation.
insights: 创新点：发现NEUROD1的双阶段调控作用
方法亮点：基因敲除和转录组分析
关键发现：NEUROD1调控神经元分化时间
insights_en: Novelty: Identified the two-phase regulatory role of NEUROD1
Method highlight: Gene knockout and transcriptomic analysis
Key finding: NEUROD1 regulates the timing of neuronal differentiation
abstract: Temporal control of neuronal differentiation is essential for establishing stable neuronal identities, yet the transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms underlying this process remain poorly understood. Using auditory neurons as an in vivo model, we investigate the role of the proneural factor NEUROD1 in regulating neuronal differentiation timing and subtype specification. To bypass early neuronal loss in germline Neurod1 deletion mutants, we generated a delayed, self-terminating conditional knockout mouse ( Neurod1ST ) that permits analysis of later differentiation stages. Integration of NEUROD1 chromatin binding and histone profiling at embryonic day (E) 11.5 with transcriptomic analyses across E11.5, E14.5, and E18.5 reveals a two-phase regulatory program during auditory neuron development that parallels dynamic Neurod1 expression. In the first phase, coinciding with Neurod1 upregulation during early neuronal differentiation, NEUROD1 preferentially binds putative enhancers of neuronal differentiation genes and promotes their transition to active chromatin states, consistent with pioneer factor activity. Loss of Neurod1 disrupts these epigenomic transitions, resulting in persistence of progenitor-like states with premature activation of differentiation and axonogenesis programs. This dysregulation is accompanied by activation of alternative regulatory networks, leading to defective neuronal migration and innervation, progressive identity instability, and apoptosis. In the second phase, marked by reexpression of Neurod1 in developing Type Ib/Ic precursors, Neurod1 deletion selectively impairs Type Ic specification while promoting a Type Ib-like identity. These findings identify NEUROD1 as a temporal regulator that coordinates developmental progression and stabilizes auditory neuron identity through phased regulatory activity, providing a mechanistic framework for how pioneer transcription factors couple chromatin remodeling to developmental timing.

title: Elastic interactions of mechanically polarizable cells
summary_zh: 研究提出机械极化细胞的弹性相互作用理论。通过分析弹性相互作用能量，发现细胞间存在短程相互作用。
summary_en: The study proposes an analytical theory of the elastic interactions of mechanically polarizable cells. By analyzing the elastic interaction energy, it finds a short-ranged interaction between cells.
insights: 创新点：提出机械极化细胞的弹性相互作用理论
方法亮点：分析弹性相互作用能量
关键发现：细胞间存在短程相互作用
insights_en: Novelty: Proposed an analytical theory of the elastic interactions of mechanically polarizable cells
Method highlight: Analyzing elastic interaction energy
Key finding: Short-ranged interaction between cells
abstract: Cells mechanically interact through the deformations they generate in their surrounding extracellular matrix. We present an analytical theory of the elastic interactions between cells that actively adapt their forces in response to local deformations of their environment. Cells are represented as localized contractile force generators, modeled as polarizable point force dipoles, whose adaptive forces are determined self-consistently with those of surrounding cells. Analysis of the associated elastic interaction energy identifies a generic short-ranged interaction arising from the mutual adaptation of cellular forces. This induced-dipole interaction is analogous to the van der Waals interaction between molecules and likewise is shown to be generally attractive for cells that enhance contractility in response to stretch. Furthermore, unlike the long-ranged elastic interaction between nonpolarizable force-dipoles, that peaks at intermediate matrix stiffness and then weakens as the matrix softens, the induced-dipole interaction strengthens monotonically as the matrix softens and can reverse the interaction from being repulsive at long cell distances to being attractive at short separations. Analytical calculations are presented to illustrate the mutual polarization of forces in pairs of interacting cells on a substrate. The identification of a generic, short-range cohesive elastic interaction between cells is important for understanding cell behavior at short separations and provides a physical mechanism driving cell accumulation on soft substrates.

title: Ocular Features of Q Fever: A Systematic Review of Case Series and Case Reports
summary_zh: 系统综述Q热眼部特征，分析病例报告和病例系列。发现Q热可导致显著视力损害。
summary_en: Systematic review of ocular features of Q fever, analyzing case reports and case series. Finds Q fever can cause significant visual morbidity.
insights: 创新点：系统综述Q热眼部特征
方法亮点：分析病例报告和病例系列
关键发现：Q热可导致视力损害
insights_en: Novelty: Systematic review of ocular features of Q fever
Method highlight: Analyzing case reports and case series
Key finding: Q fever can cause visual morbidity
abstract: Introduction: Q fever, caused by Coxiella burnetii, can manifest with ocular involvement and cause significant visual morbidity. This systematic review aims to summarise the reported ocular presentations of Q fever, treatments and clinical outcomes. Materials and Methods: The English-language literature indexed in Web of Science, Ovid Embase, and Ovid MEDLINE was systematically searched from database inception to 25 October 2026 for case reports and case series describing ocular manifestations of Q fever. Data on demographics, exposure history, ocular diagnosis, disease stage, treatment and clinical outcomes were extracted and pooled descriptively. Results: A total of 19 articles, comprising 16 case reports and 3 case series, described 28 patients with ocular manifestation of Q fever. Among the 21 cases with exposure data, 13 (61.9%) had documented occupational or environmental exposure. Intraocular inflammation was the most frequently reported manifestation (20/28, 71.4%), while nine patients presented with neuro-ophthalmic manifestations. Among 18 patients with reported clinical outcomes, 7 (38.9%) achieved recovery without reported sequelae, 8 (44.4%) showed improvement with residual abnormalities, and 3 (16.7%) experienced no improvement or deterioration. Conclusions: Q fever encompasses diverse ocular inflammatory and neuro-ophthalmic manifestations, with the posterior segment being the most commonly affected. Q fever serology may be considered in selected patients with unexplained uveitis or retinitis, particularly in endemic areas.

title: Spectacle Compliance and Associated Factors Among Adults with Refractive Error Attending a Tertiary Eye Care Center in Nepal: A Hospital-Based Cross-Sectional Study
summary_zh: 本研究评估尼泊尔三级眼科中心成人配镜依从性，分析非依从原因及相关因素。多变量回归分析显示，34.6%的参与者依从。不适感和视力模糊是主要非依从原因。
summary_en: This study assessed spectacle compliance among adults in Nepal, analyzing reasons for non-compliance and associated factors. Multivariable regression analysis showed 34.6% compliance, with discomfort and unclear vision as primary reasons for non-compliance.
insights: 创新点：首次在尼泊尔研究成人配镜依从性
方法亮点：多变量回归分析识别相关因素
关键发现：不适感和视力模糊是主要非依从原因
insights_en: Novelty: First study on spectacle compliance among adults in Nepal
Method highlight: Multivariable regression analysis identifies associated factors
Key finding: Discomfort and unclear vision are primary reasons for non-compliance
abstract: The benefit of spectacles depends on sustained use, but evidence on spectacle compliance among adults in low-resource settings is limited. This hospital-based cross-sectional study assessed self-reported compliance with prescribed spectacle wear, reasons for non-compliance, and associated factors among adults attending a tertiary eye care center in Nepal. Adults aged ≥18 years who had been prescribed spectacles at least 1 month earlier were recruited consecutively and interviewed using a structured questionnaire linked to clinical records. Associated factors were examined using multivariable logistic regression with variables selected a priori and penalized sensitivity analyses. Of 416 participants, 144 (34.6%; 95% CI 30.2–39.3%) reported compliance. Discomfort (15.8%), unclear vision (15.1%), appearance concerns (12.9%), and forgetfulness (11.8%) were the most frequent reasons for non-compliance. Compared with spectacles dispensed at the study hospital, spectacles from optical shops were consistently associated with lower odds of compliance (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 0.07, 95% CI 0.03–0.20; 0.10 after adjusting for time since the last spectacle change), whereas the association for spectacles from other hospitals (AOR 0.42, 0.25–0.71) was attenuated after this adjustment (AOR 0.54, 0.30–0.96). The association with older age was not robust. Nearly two-thirds of adults did not report using their spectacles as prescribed; dispensing quality and follow-up warrant prospective evaluation.

title: Proteins that form the nuclear pore barrier move like liquids
summary_zh: 本文研究核孔屏障蛋白的运动特性。方法上，结合活细胞测量与分子动力学模拟。实验表明，蛋白链运动灵活。
summary_en: This paper studies the movement characteristics of proteins forming the nuclear pore barrier. The method combines live cell measurements with molecular dynamics simulations. Experiments show the protein chains are highly mobile.
insights: 创新点：核孔屏障蛋白运动特性研究
方法亮点：活细胞测量与分子动力学模拟
关键发现：蛋白链运动灵活
insights_en: Novelty: Study on the movement characteristics of nuclear pore barrier proteins
Method highlight: Live cell measurements and molecular dynamics simulations
Key finding: Protein chains are highly mobile
abstract: Nuclear pores control molecular traffic into and out of the cell nucleus. Measurements in living cells, together with molecular-dynamics simulations, show that flexible protein chains that form the selectivity barriers of nuclear pores are highly mobile, and that a sugar modification and the carrier protein importin-β help to preserve this dynamic state. The motion of the nuclear pore protein NUP98 is regulated by a transport receptor and a sugar modification.

title: Multi-phase liver CT virtual contrast enhancement and diagnosis based on phase-aware diffusion network
summary_zh: 本文研究基于相位感知扩散网络的肝脏CT虚拟对比增强与诊断。方法上，提出相位特定路径分配与循环重编码学习。实验表明，模型有效。
summary_en: This paper studies liver CT virtual contrast enhancement and diagnosis based on phase-aware diffusion networks. The method proposes phase-specific path allocation and cycle re-encoding learning. Experiments show the model is effective.
insights: 创新点：相位感知扩散网络应用
方法亮点：相位特定路径分配
关键发现：模型有效
insights_en: Novelty: Application of phase-aware diffusion networks
Method highlight: Phase-specific path allocation
Key finding: Model is effective
abstract: Multi-phase contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) plays a crucial role in liver tumor diagnosis but is limited by additional radiation exposure and a restricted patient population. While virtual contrast enhancement (VCE) methods can generate virtual liver CECT images, challenges persist due to detail-deficient non-contrast CT (NCCT) images and phase-wise feature variations. In this paper, we propose phase-aware diffusion (PA-Diff), a novel model for multi-phase liver CT enhancement and contrast-agent-free liver tumor diagnosis, which combines two novel designs: 1) Phase-specific path allocation that enables precise multi-phase enhancement by combining independent diffusion paths and shared encoder and decoder; 2) Cycle re-encoding learning that enhances tumor detail by recovering target images and re-encoding them into complementary features for loss calculation during training. We also perform automatic diagnosis on the VCE CT images. Experiments on two dataset demonstrate effective multi-phase enhancement and accurate Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) screening and Microvascular Invasion (MVI) diagnosis, highlighting the model's clinical value.

title: Clinical-SAM: Agentic Test-Time Adaptation of SAM via Physician-in-the-Loop for Clinical Tumor Segmentation
summary_zh: 提出Clinical-SAM，解决SAM模型在临床部署中的泛化问题。采用两阶段代理医生参与式TTA框架，无需空间标注。实验表明，该方法有效提高了肿瘤分割的准确性。
summary_en: Proposes Clinical-SAM to address the generalization issue of SAM models in clinical deployment. Utilizes a two-phase agentic physician-in-the-loop TTA framework without spatial annotations. Experiments show that this method effectively improves the accuracy of tumor segmentation.
insights: 创新点：提出代理医生参与式TTA框架
方法亮点：无需空间标注，降低标注负担
关键发现：提高了肿瘤分割的准确性
insights_en: Novelty: Proposes an agentic physician-in-the-loop TTA framework
Method highlight: No need for spatial annotations, reduces annotation burden
Key finding: Improves the accuracy of tumor segmentation
abstract: Interactive foundation models such as SAM struggle to generalize across clinical deployment sites. Among existing adaptation strategies, test-time adaptation (TTA) is the most promising, yet current TTA methods trade one problem for another: removing the physician eliminates clinical grounding, while retaining the physician reintroduces a costly annotation burden. In this work, we propose Clinical-SAM, a two-phase agentic physician-in-the-loop TTA framework that teaches a frozen SAM to approximate what a physician would accept - directly and continuously, without requiring spatial annotations. In Phase I (pre-deployment), a self-prompting agent trained via reinforcement learning generates prompts autonomously, eliminating per-case expert spatial input at inference. In Phase II (deployment), the agent policy is refined online by the one signal physicians already produce: a binary accept/reject feedback on each proposed mask. As the binary feedback accumulates across deployed cases, the agent converges toward a policy that produces masks meeting a reference acceptance standard designed to approximate physician judgment, with progressively fewer interactions. We evaluate Clinical-SAM in a pre-clinical setting on six oncological benchmarks spanning CT (colon, pancreas, liver, kidney) and PET (head & neck, lung) tumor segmentation, using agreement with reference-standard segmentations as a proxy for physician acceptance. Clinical-SAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on all six datasets, outperforming fine-tuning, interactive, TTA, and online-learning baselines, while requiring only 3.3 binary judgments per case on average across the six datasets. Our code is available here.

title: CPCLNet: Advancing Cross-Modal Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation with Clustering-Inspired Prototype Consistency Learning
summary_zh: 提出CPCLNet，解决跨模态FSMIS中的模态差异问题。通过原型一致性学习，提高特征空间一致性、原型可靠性和亲和图一致性。实验表明，该方法有效提高了分割准确性。
summary_en: Proposes CPCLNet to address the modality discrepancy problem in cross-modal FSMIS. By prototype consistency learning, it improves feature space consistency, prototype reliability, and affinity map coherence. Experiments show that this method effectively improves segmentation accuracy.
insights: 创新点：提出原型一致性学习解决模态差异
方法亮点：提高特征空间一致性，增强分割能力
关键发现：显著提高分割准确性
insights_en: Novelty: Proposes prototype consistency learning to solve modality discrepancy
Method highlight: Improves feature space consistency, enhances segmentation capability
Key finding: Significantly improves segmentation accuracy
abstract: Cross-modal few-shot medical image segmentation (FSMIS) provides a solution for alleviating annotation scarcity and improving generalization across imaging modalities. However, severe modality discrepancy can disrupt support-query matching, contaminate support-derived foreground and background prototypes, and produce noisy affinity maps, making target-modality segmentation unreliable. To address this problem, we propose CPCLNet, a clustering-inspired prototype consistency learning network for cross-modal FSMIS. CPCLNet formulates cross-modal segmentation as a prototype consistency learning problem and progressively improves feature-space consistency, prototype reliability, and affinity-map coherence. Specifically, a parameter-sharing feature encoder provides a common representation basis across modalities, and a cross-modal distribution alignment module performs episode-specific support-query alignment. A clustering-inspired representative prototype descriptor further suppresses unstable support responses and constructs compact, modality-robust prototypes. Finally, an RWKV-based affinity map prediction module propagates prototype-guided correspondence across long-range spatial contexts with linear complexity. Extensive experiments on three imaging modalities, demonstrate that CPCLNet outperforms existing methods, achieving an average Dice improvement of 3.34 percentage points over the second-best competitor across CT→MRI and CT→PET tasks under both 1-shot and 5-shot settings. Further integration with MedSAM yields consistent improvements, indicating CP-CLNet's complementary potential with foundation models.

title: Fluid eMTBR-tau243 as a Biomarker of Mixed 3-Repeat and 4-Repeat Tau Pathology
summary_zh: 评估生物流体eMTBR-tau243在tauopathies中的应用，发现其在非AD tauopathies中的特异性及生物意义。
summary_en: This study evaluates the application of biofluid eMTBR-tau243 in tauopathies, finding its specificity and biological significance in non-AD tauopathies.
insights: 创新点：eMTBR-tau243在tauopathies中的新应用
方法亮点：采用病例对照研究设计
关键发现：eMTBR-tau243在非AD tauopathies中的特异性
insights_en: Novelty: New application of eMTBR-tau243 in tauopathies
Method highlight: Using a case-control study design
Key finding: Specificity of eMTBR-tau243 in non-AD tauopathies
abstract: Importance: Neurodegenerative diseases with abnormal tau protein aggregation in the brain (ie, tauopathies) can be classified by the tau isoform that accumulates: 3-repeat (3R), 4-repeat (4R), or mixed 3R/4R tauopathies, which include chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), some forms of frontotemporal lobar degeneration, and Alzheimer disease (AD). The endogenously cleaved form of tau microtubule binding region containing the residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) can be detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood and has been associated with AD tau pathology, but its specificity and biological interpretation in non-AD tauopathies remains unclear. Objective: To evaluate biofluid eMTBR-tau243 in a range of tauopathies. Design, Setting, and Participants: This case-control study included 4 biorepositories based in the US that contributed CSF and plasma samples from participants with and without tauopathies, many of whom had antemortem biofluid samples paired with autopsy or genetically defined neuropathology. Samples were analyzed between August 2023 and December 2025. Data analysis occurred from August 2024 to July 2026. Exposure: CSF and plasma eMTBR-tau243 concentrations measured using a mass spectrometry-based assay. Main Outcomes and Measures: Outcomes included mixed 3R/4R tauopathy (eg, AD and CTE) based on autopsy, frontotemporal lobar degeneration with MAPT variants (FTLD-MAPT), and CTE stage. Differences in biomarker levels between groups were evaluated using analysis of variance or analysis of covariance, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was calculated to evaluate the discriminative performance of fluid eMTBR-tau243. Results: Among the 229 participants (196 with CSF samples and 55 with plasma samples [22 with both]), mean (SD) age at fluid sample collection was 63 (13) years and 108 (47%) were female. Median (IQR) CSF eMTBR-tau243 was increased in 10 patients with AD (0.459 [0.246-0.801] fmol/mL) compared with 29 cognitively unimpaired controls (0.002 [0.001-0.005] fmol/mL) (adjusted P < .001), but other autopsy-confirmed non-AD tauopathies (which included 52 individuals with conditions including progressive supranuclear palsy and corticobasal degeneration) did not demonstrate an increase (0.015 [0.008, 0.039] fmol/mL). Six symptomatic FTLD-MAPT variant carriers with mixed 3R/4R tauopathy (R406W, V337M, and G389R) had increased median (IQR) CSF eMTBR-tau243 (0.140 [0.055-0.174] fmol/mL) compared with 15 4R tauopathy variant carriers including N279K and P301L (0.004 [0.001-0.044] fmol/mL) (P = .001). Median (IQR) plasma eMTBR-tau243 was increased in 11 patients with CTE (1.93 [0.42-3.68] fmol/L) compared with 20 cognitively unimpaired controls (0.29 [0.05-0.62] fmol/L) (adjusted P = .007), but did not increase as high as among 14 patients with AD (11.25 [2.29-19.38] fmol/L). Plasma eMTBR-tau243 distinguished CTE stage III and IV from controls (AUC, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.92-1.00), but not CTE stage I from controls (AUC, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.32-0.97). Conclusions and Relevance: This study found that plasma and CSF eMTBR-tau243 were increased in mixed 3R/4R tauopathies including AD, high-stage CTE, and a subset of genetic FTLD-MAPT, compared with cognitively unimpaired controls. Further validation in larger cohorts is needed to determine the clinical utility of eMTBR-tau243 as a potential diagnostic biomarker for CTE and other tauopathies beyond AD.

title: Tale of Two Estimands: Distinguishing What Is Observed From What Is Inferred
Once-Weekly Ribupatide for Weight Loss in Adults in China With Overweight or Obesity: Research Summary
Pediatric Obesity Pharmacotherapy: From Therapeutic Scarcity to Therapeutic Choice
Tirzepatide in Adolescents With Obesity: Research Summary
Elastic tricriticality at the collapse of magnetic order in a valence fluctuating Eu-based compound
summary_zh: 研究Eu基化合物中磁序崩溃的弹性三临界性，揭示晶体弹性与电子关联的强耦合。
summary_en: This study investigates the elastic tricriticality at the collapse of magnetic order in a valence fluctuating Eu-based compound, revealing strong coupling between crystal elasticity and electronic correlations.
insights: 创新点：揭示晶体弹性与电子关联的强耦合
方法亮点：采用单晶实验方法
关键发现：弹性三临界性的存在
insights_en: Novelty: Revealing strong coupling between crystal elasticity and electronic correlations
Method highlight: Using single crystal experimental methods
Key finding: Existence of elastic tricriticality
abstract: Spin and charge fluctuations are key for understanding the properties of materials with strongly correlated electrons, but their coupling to the atomic crystal lattice is often assumed to be weak and perturbative. In this work, we demonstrate that at tricritical points (TCPs), that are associated with electronic correlations, a coupling to crystal elasticity is generically nonperturbative. It will modify the tricritical universality class leading to elastic tricriticality , characterized by a compressibility that diverges in a universal manner with the correlation length. To test this scenario experimentally, we use single crystals of EuPd 2 (Si 1− x Ge x ) 2 where, depending on x and pressure, magnetic order collapses due to strong valence fluctuations. First, we confirm the presence of a TCP for x ≈ 0.1 by using complementary probes, in particular, measurements of relative length changes under control of temperature and He-gas pressure. Second, by studying the elastic response, we uncover clear signatures of elastic tricriticality, notably a drastically enhanced compressibility.

title: BioLM-Score: Language-Prior Conditioned Probabilistic Geometric Potentials for Protein-Ligand Scoring
summary_zh: 提出BioLM-Score模型，通过结合蛋白质和分子语言模型嵌入，提高蛋白质-配体评分的准确性。
summary_en: This study proposes the BioLM-Score model, integrating frozen protein and molecular language-model embeddings to improve the accuracy of protein-ligand scoring.
insights: 创新点：结合蛋白质和分子语言模型嵌入
方法亮点：采用门控图卷积技术
关键发现：评分准确性提高
insights_en: Novelty: Integrating frozen protein and molecular language-model embeddings
Method highlight: Using gated graph convolution techniques
Key finding: Improved scoring accuracy
abstract: MOTIVATION: Protein-ligand scoring must address affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening, but these objectives are not necessarily optimized together. Geometric likelihood models may generalize poorly when training-set structural coverage is limited. We test whether pretrained biomolecular representations improve scoring under a controlled geometric baseline. RESULTS: BioLM-Score integrates frozen protein and molecular language-model embeddings into a residue-atom distance-likelihood framework via gated graph convolutions. We evaluate geometry-only, jointly trained, and two-stage fine-tuned variants, using the jointly trained variant for the primary controlled comparisons. All three DEKOIS 2.0 screening endpoints improve over the matched geometric baseline with target-level paired support, but affinity scoring and ranking do not improve uniformly. Under a time-split protocol, scoring is significantly lower and ranking is also lower than the geometric baseline, while screening gains persist. On BDB2020+, the difference in affinity correlation between BioLM-Score and GenScore narrows after LP-PDBBind-compatible retraining. Shuffling protein embeddings at inference reduces the screening advantage. However, retrained shuffle controls recover much of the performance, so correct alignment is not established as necessary. BioLM-Score strengthens geometric scoring on screening tasks without retraining the language models. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: Code, dataset-split identifiers, preprocessing and evaluation scripts, and language-model embedding-generation utilities are available at https://github.com/SZU-ADDG/BioLM-Score. An archival code snapshot and pretrained model weights are available at doi:10.5281/zenodo.21878818. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: Addendum: A meta-analysis of GFR slope as a surrogate endpoint for kidney failure
A Topology-Feature Disentangled Deep Clustering Method for scRNA-seq Based on Graph-to-MLP Distillation
summary_zh: 本研究提出一种基于图到MLP蒸馏的拓扑特征解耦深度聚类方法，用于scRNA-seq数据。方法上，结合AdaBoost原理。实验表明，该方法有效利用了scRNA-seq数据中的表达谱和拓扑信息。
summary_en: This study proposes a topology-feature disentangled deep clustering method for scRNA-seq based on graph-to-MLP distillation, incorporating AdaBoost principles. Experiments show that this method effectively utilizes expression profiles and topological information within scRNA-seq data.
insights: 创新点：提出拓扑特征解耦深度聚类方法。
方法亮点：结合AdaBoost原理。
关键发现：有效利用scRNA-seq数据。
insights_en: Novelty: Proposes a topology-feature disentangled deep clustering method.
Method highlight: Incorporates AdaBoost principles.
Key finding: Effectively utilizes scRNA-seq data.
abstract: MOTIVATION: Graph neural networks (GNNs), owing to their ability to model topological relationships between cells, have gradually emerged as a mainstream approach in the clustering analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. However, their practical application still faces the following challenges: (1) excessive smoothing undermines cellular heterogeneity; (2) pre-constructed graphs introduce end-to-end dependencies; (3) large-scale cellular graph computations are computationally intensive. RESULTS: To fully utilise the expression profiles and topological information contained within scRNA-seq data and overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a Graph-to-MLP (G2M) knowledge distillation method incorporating AdaBoost principles, and builds upon this to develop a graph-disentangled single-cell clustering framework-scAdaG2M. This framework utilises a GNN teacher model to learn higher-order topological relationships and local neighbourhood structures between cells on a cellular graph, whilst multiple lightweight MLP student models perform feature learning in an ungraphed setting. By combining this with an AdaBoost-style dynamic reweighting strategy, the framework enhances the model's ability to characterise cells that are difficult to distinguish, cells with blurred boundaries, and potentially rare cell populations, thereby mitigating the dilution of cellular heterogeneity caused by over-smoothing. At the same time, this framework effectively decouples graph-based modelling from graph-free reasoning, reduces the end-to-end reliance on pre-constructed graphs, and significantly reduces the computational overhead associated with large-scale cellular graphs. AVAILABILITY: All datasets used in this study are publicly available. Detailed information about all the single-cell datasets analyzed in this paper is provided in Supplementary Table 1. The source code is available at https://github.com/gxl1110/scAdaG2M and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21512950. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: Data-Driven Modeling of Promoter Affection to 5’ Untranslated Region Design for Rational Predictive Translational Engineering
summary_zh: 研究基因启动子对5'UTR的影响，构建预测模型，揭示转录与翻译调控的相互作用。
summary_en: Investigates the effect of promoters on 5' UTR, constructs predictive models, and reveals the interaction between transcription and translation regulation.
insights: 创新点：构建预测模型预测翻译工程
方法亮点：结合生物物理模型和序列库分析
关键发现：启动子影响翻译速率和mRNA二级结构
insights_en: Novelty: Constructs predictive models for translational engineering
Method highlight: Combines biophysical models with sequence library analysis
Key finding: Promoters affect translation rates and mRNA secondary structures
abstract: MOTIVATION: Precise gene expression control is fundamental for biological research and synthetic systems. While biophysical models predict transcriptional or translational regulation, they often overlook their potential interplay. Combining these regulations offers synergistic control, but its influence remains incompletely understood. RESULTS: Here, we investigated how promoter replacement affects 5' untranslated region (5' UTR)-mediated translation while designing the sequence of Escherichia coli. Using predictive models and a comprehensive library of promoter-5' UTR pairs, we characterized the interference of promoters with translation rates in terms of mRNA secondary structures, especially the alternative folding of the Shine-Dalgarno (SD) region and frequency of the major transcription start sites (TSSs), which leads to the misprediction of gene expression. AVAILABILITY: Based on this, we developed UTR Designer Pro, a model for designing promoter-5' UTR sequences with higher accuracy, now available as a web service at https://sbi.postech.ac.kr/utr_designer_pro/. Our work improves understanding of transcriptional and translational regulation, aiding gene expression control in bacterial systems. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: ReMoD-Mol: Reliability-Aware Multimodal Learning with Descriptor-Guided Knowledge Distillation for Molecular Property Prediction
summary_zh: 提出ReMoD-Mol框架，解决分子属性预测中的信息冗余和物理化学先验不足问题。
summary_en: Proposes the ReMoD-Mol framework to address information redundancy and insufficient physicochemical priors in molecular property prediction.
insights: 创新点：可靠性感知的多模态学习
方法亮点：描述符引导的知识蒸馏
关键发现：提高分子属性预测的准确性
insights_en: Novelty: Reliability-aware multimodal learning
Method highlight: Descriptor-guided knowledge distillation
Key finding: Improved accuracy in molecular property prediction
abstract: MOTIVATION: Accurate molecular property prediction (MPP) remains a central challenge in drug discovery. Given the limited availability of labeled molecular data, multimodal molecular representation learning offers a promising means of integrating complementary structural information for MPP. Existing multimodal models still face two limitations: (i) common fusion strategies, particularly direct concatenation, can introduce redundant information or signals that are weakly relevant to the target property; and (ii) the effective incorporation of complementary physicochemical priors into multimodal representations remains insufficiently explored. RESULTS: Here, we proposed ReMoD-Mol, a reliability-aware multimodal framework that integrated molecular graphs, SMILES sequences and two-dimensional molecular images. Task-adaptive modality calibration learned one set of weights per benchmark from downstream supervision to regulate the relative contributions of the three molecular views. Descriptor- and fingerprint-based teachers further provided task-conditioned chemical priors through train-only, five-fold out-of-fold knowledge distillation. Prototype-guided embedding shaping together with graph-view and SMILES-view consistency objectives regularized the fused representation space. Across nine MoleculeNet benchmark datasets spanning regression and classification, ReMoD-Mol achieved the best mean performance on seven datasets and the second-best on the other two in a scaffold-split comparison with 14 baselines. Representation analyses revealed smoother property-related manifolds and more discriminative class structures, while learned modality coefficients exhibited distinct task-dependent fusion patterns. Teacher-prior and ablation analyses further supported the complementary roles of chemical-prior transfer and multi-view representation regularization. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: Source code, processed datasets and implementation details are publicly available at https://github.com/27167199/ReMoD-Mol.

Chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 participates in the internalization of arginine-rich dipeptide repeat proteins
summary_zh: 研究硫酸软骨素蛋白聚糖4在富含精氨酸的二肽重复蛋白内化中的作用。
summary_en: Studies the role of chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 in the internalization of arginine-rich dipeptide repeat proteins.
insights: 创新点：揭示硫酸软骨素蛋白聚糖4的内化机制
方法亮点：使用细胞和小分子方法
关键发现：温度依赖的内吞作用机制
insights_en: Novelty: Reveals the internalization mechanism of chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4
Method highlight: Uses cellular and small molecule approaches
Key finding: Temperature-dependent endocytosis mechanism
abstract: Microsatellite repeat expansion of the 5′ GGGGCC 3′ sequence in the C9orf72 gene is the most common monogenic form of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia. Dipeptide repeat proteins (DPRs) translated from the mutant allele can be detected in postmortem brains of afflicted individuals. The arginine containing peptides, poly proline-arginine (poly-PR) and poly glycine-arginine (poly-GR), are particularly noxious to cells. Both can undergo cell-to-cell transmission, but underlying mechanisms are not understood. We found rapid internalization and nucleolar localization of bath-applied hemagglutinin (HA) tagged poly-PR with twenty repeats (HA-PR 20 ) in cell lines and neurons. Small molecule and RNAi approaches implicated a temperature-dependent, fluid phase endocytosis mechanism for HA-PR 20 . We sought to identify DPR-related cell surface uptake factors using µMap high-resolution proximity labeling. DPR–iridium conjugates identified candidate cell-surface proteins which were interrogated in a secondary RNAi screen. Focusing on our strongest candidate, chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 (CSPG4), we showed cellular uptake of HA-PR 20 is reduced by inhibition of glycosaminoglycan chain synthesis and knockdown or ablation of CSPG4. Knockdown of CSPG4 protected PR 20 -induced neuronal toxicity. Using a dual reporter system to interrogate in vitro neuron-to-neuron transmission of PR 50, we found PR 50 synthesized by one neuron readily spread to neighboring cells. Transmission was significantly reduced with CSPG4 knockdown. Similarly conditioned media from PR 50 or GR 50 expressing neurons contained transmissible protein that was internalized into neurons in a CSPG4-dependent manner. These results suggest CSPG4 participates in poly-PR/poly-GR internalization and transmission.

title: Supercritical snapping and controlled launching via dual-latch gels
summary_zh: 报告双卡扣凝胶实现超临界断裂和可控发射。
summary_en: Reports supercritical snapping and controlled launching via dual-latch gels.
insights: 创新点：双卡扣凝胶设计实现超临界断裂
方法亮点：调节能量输出和断裂路径
关键发现：凝胶的厚度影响能量储存和释放
insights_en: Novelty: Dual-latch gel design enables supercritical snapping
Method highlight: Regulates energy output and snapping pathways
Key finding: Gel thickness affects energy storage and release
abstract: Natural organisms have evolved integrated Latch-Mediated Spring Actuation systems (LaMSA) that consist of multiple latches and springs to enhance power output and adapt to diverse environmental conditions. Similar designs are appealing yet largely unexplored in engineered materials due to the complexity of integrating multiple components into a single material platform. Here, we report a dual-latch magneto-elastic shell device capable of selectively activating the latches to regulate snapping pathways and energy output based on specific actuation requirements. Differential deswelling across the thickness acts as the “motor” to load the elastic energy into the shell, which is then released via the snap-through instability once the loading reaches the critical threshold, constituting an intrinsic mechanical latch. Activation of the external magnetic latch delays snapping onset beyond the threshold of the intrinsic latch, leading to a power-amplified supercritical snap-through instability as well as a bifurcation instability. The combined function of both latches allows for flexible control over energy storage and release. Additionally, this integrated LaMSA system possesses an untethered anchoring mechanism, enabling the device to launch in arbitrary directions from the substrate, driven by the energy released during snapping. We envision that the design principles of dual-latch LaMSA systems will create opportunities for power-dense actuation in engineered materials and robotic devices.

title: Distinct nanoscale architectures of GABAergic inhibitory synapses predict diverse synaptic output
summary_zh: 研究GABA能抑制性突触的纳米级结构预测不同的突触输出。
summary_en: Studies the nanoscale architecture of GABAergic inhibitory synapses predicting diverse synaptic outputs.
insights: 创新点：关注GABA能突触的纳米结构
方法亮点：结合突触结构和功能
关键发现：纳米柱结构增强突触效能
insights_en: Novelty: Focuses on the nanoscale architecture of GABAergic synapses
Method highlight: Combines synaptic structure and function
Key finding: Nanocolumn structures enhance synaptic efficacy
abstract: GABAergic synaptic inhibition is heterogenous across neuronal compartments, and plays a critical role in shaping local, cellular, and circuit excitability. In pyramidal neurons, inhibition is mediated by GABA A receptors (GABA A Rs) clustered at the inhibitory postsynaptic domain (iPSD). Synaptic strength depends not only on the number of GABA A Rs within the iPSD, but also on their precise nanoscale organization into discrete subsynaptic domains (SSDs). These SSDs often align with presynaptic GABA release sites to form nanocolumn structures that enhance synaptic efficacy. While nanocolumn organization is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of synaptic function, most studies of GABAergic synapses have focused on archetypal dendritic synapses, which control the plasticity and integration of excitatory inputs. Nonetheless, it remains unclear whether somatic synapses—which deliver robust inhibition to suppress neuronal output—share a similar nanoarchitecture. Here, we used complementary superresolution imaging approaches to directly compare inhibitory synapses in somatic and dendritic compartments. We found that somatic synapses are larger and exhibit greater structural diversity and nanoscale complexity than dendritic synapses. Dendritic synapses display relatively compact architectures with GABA A R SSDs frequently arranged into nanocolumns. In contrast, somatic synapses show a broader range of organizations, including aligned nanocolumns as well as more disorganized configurations with misaligned release sites or receptor SSDs, arrangements that likely exhibit input-specificity. Computational modeling revealed that these structural differences produce distinct functional outcomes, including increased inhibitory postsynaptic current amplitude and altered kinetics at somatic synapses. Together, our findings demonstrate that nanoscale organization differentially shapes inhibitory strength and signaling properties across neuronal compartments.

title: Music illuminates sociocultural dimensions of autobiographical memory
summary_zh: 研究音乐如何揭示自传记忆的社会文化维度。通过分析大学本科生对熟悉歌曲的回忆，发现音乐与特定生活阶段和社会文化行为模式相关。
summary_en: This study explores how music reveals the sociocultural dimensions of autobiographical memory. Analysis of undergraduates' memories of familiar songs reveals connections to specific life stages and socially and culturally shaped behavior patterns.
insights: 创新点：音乐作为社会文化身份的标记在自传记忆中的作用被揭示。
方法亮点：自然语言处理用于分析音乐激发的回忆内容。
关键发现：音乐与特定生活阶段和社会文化行为模式相关。
insights_en: Novelty: The role of music as a marker of social and cultural identity in autobiographical memory is revealed.
Method highlight: Natural language processing is used to analyze the content of memories evoked by music.
Key finding: Music is related to specific life stages and socially and culturally shaped behavior patterns.
abstract: Researchers have long theorized that autobiographical memory relies on sociocultural structures, such as life scripts and event schemas. The potency of music as a marker of social and personal identity, combined with its ubiquity in everyday life, allows us to connect these everyday scripts to larger patterns of socially and culturally shaped behavior. We collected free-response descriptions of autobiographical memories evoked by short clips of familiar songs from university undergraduates (n = 233). The songs spanned three popular genres and aligned with two significant periods of listeners’ lives. We analyzed the similarities and differences in the content of memories for particular songs using natural language processing. Memories cued by songs from the same category displayed striking similarities, suggesting that particular types of music cue memories that are similar between listeners but that vary according to characteristics such as music genre and release date. Two control conditions, in which a new set of participants reported memories evoked by key words from the lyrics (n = 121) and short narrative summaries of the lyrics (n = 129), indicate that these results cannot be explained by within-category similarities in the songs’ lyrical content. Instead, we suggest that the intersubjective structure of music-evoked autobiographical memories reflects socioculturally-defined scripts tied to song characteristics such as genre and release date. Thus, while memories may feel idiosyncratic and personal, there are also substantial similarities in life experiences between individuals with broadly similar backgrounds, and these shared experiences can be spontaneously called to mind through the seemingly innocuous act of turning on the radio.
