The experimentally calibrated computational model provides a tool to predict the effect of crack-parallel tension on the changes of load capacity and of the effective fracture energy of knitted polymer composites, enabling rational design of these composites in engineering applications such as wearables and soft robotics.

title: Vegetation decay enhances terrestrial nitrous acid emissions through nitrate reduction
summary_zh: 研究识别植物残体分解产生的HONO作为陆地HONO排放的新来源。通过植被硝酸盐、凋落物分解、土壤和气候数据估计HONO排放。
summary_en: This study identifies HONO emissions from decaying aboveground plant residues as a new source of terrestrial HONO emissions. HONO emissions from vegetation decay are estimated using global datasets on vegetation nitrate, litter decomposition, soil, and climate.
insights: 创新点：识别植物残体分解产生的HONO
方法亮点：利用双同位素追踪
关键发现：植被凋落物分解是HONO排放的重要来源
insights_en: Novelty: Identification of HONO from plant residue decomposition
Method highlight: Use of dual-isotope tracing
Key finding: Vegetation decay is an important source of HONO emissions
abstract: Photolysis of nitrous acid (HONO) drives ozone and secondary aerosol formation, yet its sources remain poorly constrained. We identify HONO emissions from decaying aboveground plant residues as a previously overlooked plant-derived component of terrestrial HONO emissions. Field observations and dual-isotope (15 N– 18 O) tracing reveal that HONO arises mainly from nitrate reduction within decomposing plants. We integrated global datasets on vegetation nitrate, litter decomposition, soil, and climate to estimate HONO emissions from vegetation decay at 1.1 ± 0.1 Tg N y −1. This substantially narrows the long-standing uncertainty in HONO budget. This plant-mediated pathway extends the soil-atmosphere paradigm to soil-plant-atmosphere framework. Moreover, we identify emission hotspots and drivers, assess their climate-driven shifts, and propose region-specific mitigation strategies. These findings uncover a missing link between terrestrial nitrogen cycling and atmospheric reactivity, highlighting biogeochemical controls on air quality.

title: Precursor-engineered lithiation kinetics enable low-temperature synthesis of Li–Ni–O positive electrode materials
summary_zh: 研究通过工程化前驱体形态和结晶度调节层状相的成核和生长。使用高比表面积的NiO和Ni(OH)2纳米片以缩短Li+扩散长度。
summary_en: This study regulates the nucleation and growth of the layered phase by engineering the morphology and crystallinity of the precursors. Nanosheets of NiO and Ni(OH)2 with high specific surface areas are used to shorten Li+ diffusion lengths.
insights: 创新点：低温度合成Li-Ni-O正极材料
方法亮点：工程化前驱体形态和结晶度
关键发现：缩短Li+扩散长度
insights_en: Novelty: Low-temperature synthesis of Li-Ni-O positive electrode materials
Method highlight: Engineering of precursor morphology and crystallinity
Key finding: Shortening Li+ diffusion lengths
abstract: High-nickel cathodes provide high capacity in lithium-ion batteries; however, their slow lithiation reactions require a prolonged high-temperature hold during synthesis which is directly responsible for high manufacturing cost. Here, we report that the precursor morphology and crystallinity can be engineered to regulate the nucleation and growth of the layered phase at temperatures as low as 575 °C. We use nanosheets of NiO and Ni(OH) 2 with high specific surface areas to maximize the contact area between Li and Ni precursors and to shorten Li + diffusion lengths. Highly crystalline NiO seeds early and uniform layered phase nucleation at low temperatures. Preheating Ni(OH) 2 to NiO at 300 °C maintains the large surface area and yields a higher layered fraction with limited lamellae coarsening. Preheating at 500 °C produces more crystalline NiO seeds that promote the synchronous Ni oxidation and cation ordering upon layered phase formation to deliver higher discharge capacity and better rate capability than conventionally synthesized LiNiO 2. In contrast, along the hydroxide-based route, in situ generated Li 2 CO 3 disrupts wetting and hampers lithiation, ultimately trapping lithium within a disordered rocksalt intermediate. This work demonstrates that precursor morphology, crystallinity, and processing temperature control lithiation kinetics, providing broad guidance for energy-efficient synthesizing advanced oxide battery cathodes.

title: Interploidy massively increases meiotic crossovers in pericentromeric recombination deserts
summary_zh: 研究显示异源多倍体显著增加着丝粒重组沙漠中的减数分裂交叉。通过杂交产生异源多倍体，并观察到类似的不规则减数分裂。
summary_en: This study shows that interploidy hybridization significantly increases meiotic crossovers in pericentromeric recombination deserts. Heteroploid hybrids were produced by crossing, and similar meiotic deregulation was observed.
insights: 创新点：异源多倍体增加减数分裂交叉
方法亮点：杂交产生异源多倍体
关键发现：观察到类似的不规则减数分裂
insights_en: Novelty: Interploidy hybridization increases meiotic crossovers
Method highlight: Production of heteroploid hybrids by crossing
Key finding: Similar meiotic deregulation observed
abstract: Meiotic recombination reshuffles genetic diversity through reciprocal DNA exchanges between chromosomes known as crossovers. In most eukaryotes, crossovers are highly constrained in both frequency and distribution, leaving large genomic regions with little or no recombination. A notable exception is the Brassica AAC allotriploid hybrid obtained from a cross between allotetraploid Brassica napus (AACC) and diploid Brassica rapa (AA), which exhibits elevated recombination and crossover formation near centromeres. Here, we generated a CCA allotriploid hybrid from a cross between B. napus and Brassica oleracea (CC), and subsequently produced AAC allotriploids by crossing the CCA hybrid with B. rapa. Both CCA and AAC allotriploids exhibit similar meiotic deregulation, demonstrating that this phenomenon is not restricted to AAC hybrids. Both systems displayed a marked increase in crossover frequency within normally low-recombining chromosome regions, reaching 9.4-fold in AAC and 13.4-fold in CCA allotriploids. Alternating CCA and AAC allotriploids efficiently reshuffled both B. napus subgenomes within only two generations. Using genetic mapping and cytogenetics, we further identified homoeologous exchanges. Remarkably, crossovers occurring on chromosomes involved in homoeologous associations exhibited a more pronounced redistribution toward nonrecombining regions than those on homologously paired chromosomes. Moreover, the frequency of homoeologous associations varied with the diploid progenitor genotype, indicating that genetic factors controlling homoeologous recombination already exist in Brassica diploids. Altogether, our results identify allotriploidy as a simple and powerful strategy to unlock recombination deserts, which harbor 21% of total resistance gene analogs, and provide insights into its potential role in allopolyploid evolution, adaptation, and speciation.

title: A herbivore-induced plant volatile facilitates group foraging in locusts
summary_zh: 研究证明植物挥发性化合物S-linalool促进蝗虫的群居觅食。通过基因编辑使嗅觉受体非功能化，消除了电生理和行为吸引。
summary_en: This study demonstrates that the induced volatile S-linalool promotes group foraging in locusts. Electrophysiological responses and behavioral attraction were abolished by genome editing to make the olfactory receptor nonfunctional.
insights: 创新点：植物挥发性化合物促进蝗虫觅食
方法亮点：基因编辑研究嗅觉受体
关键发现：S-linalool作为强吸引剂
insights_en: Novelty: Plant volatile promotes locust foraging
Method highlight: Genome editing to study olfactory receptors
Key finding: S-linalool as a potent attractant
abstract: Plants have evolved sophisticated defense strategies against herbivory, often releasing volatile compounds upon attack to deter further feeding. Here, we demonstrate the induced volatile S-linalool promotes phase- and stage-specific group foraging in the migratory locust (Locusta migratoria). We show that S-linalool, a volatile whose emission increases more than 10-fold following damage by gregarious nymphs, acts as a potent attractant that drives other nymphs to aggregate and feed on previously attacked rice plants. Mechanistically, we identified the olfactory receptor LmOR49 that detects S-linalool and used genome editing to make this receptor nonfunctional, thereby abolishing both electrophysiological responses and behavioral attraction. We also inactivated rice genes required for S-linalool biosynthesis, abolishing its emission, rendering plants unattractive, and disrupting locust feeding preference. Although feeding on previously attacked plants provides no detectable direct fitness benefit under our experimental conditions, prior locust feeding suppresses the accumulation of deterrent metabolites, potentially increasing plant palatability for subsequent feeding. S-linalool thus serves as an olfactory cue that guides gregarious nymphs toward previously attacked, more palatable plants. Collectively, these findings uncover a comprehensive mechanism whereby a plant defense volatile is exploited by an insect herbivore to promote group foraging, broadening our understanding of plant–insect interactions and suggesting molecular targets for locust control.

title: Ctf4 chaperones parental histones to preserve epigenetic memory
summary_zh: 研究确定Ctf4作为组蛋白伴侣，直接调控父代组蛋白转移以保持表观遗传继承。Ctf4的N端结构域包含特定的组蛋白结合基序。
summary_en: This study identifies Ctf4 as a histone chaperone that directly orchestrates the transfer of parental histones to preserve epigenetic inheritance. The N-terminal domain of Ctf4 harbors a specific histone-binding motif.
insights: 创新点：Ctf4作为组蛋白伴侣
方法亮点：研究Ctf4的N端结构域
关键发现：Ctf4与Tof1结合
insights_en: Novelty: Ctf4 as a histone chaperone
Method highlight: Study of the N-terminal domain of Ctf4
Key finding: Ctf4 binds to Tof1
abstract: Faithful transmission of chromatin states through cell division requires symmetric transfer of parental histones to daughter strands, yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identify the replisome scaffold Ctf4 as a bona fide histone chaperone that directly orchestrates parental histone transfer to preserve epigenetic inheritance. We show that the N-terminal domain (NTD) of Ctf4 harbors a specific histone-binding motif (HBM) embedded within its intrinsically disordered linker region. This HBM engages the DNA-binding surface of histone H3 and, in concert with Spt16 and Mcm2, transiently tethers parental histone hexamer onto Tof1 at the advancing replisome, priming them for subsequent transfer to nascent DNA. Disrupting Ctf4-HBM severely compromises parental histone sequestration, misdirects their recycling away from the lagging strand, and causes substantial loss of gene silencing at heterochromatic loci. Our findings establish Ctf4 not merely as a structural scaffold, but as a central chaperone at the replication fork that actively governs symmetric partitioning of parental histones, thereby ensuring the fidelity of epigenetic memory through successive cell divisions.

title: PRMT5 licenses AARS1-dependent histone lactylation to amplify microglial glycolytic reprogramming in neuropathic pain
summary_zh: 研究揭示PRMT5通过AARS1依赖性组蛋白乳酸化放大神经性疼痛中微胶质糖酵解重编程。阻断AARS1核定位损害组蛋白乳酸化和糖酵解反应。
summary_en: This study reveals that PRMT5 amplifies microglial glycolytic reprogramming in neuropathic pain through AARS1-dependent histone lactylation. Disrupting AARS1 nuclear localization impairs histone lactylation and glycolytic responses.
insights: 创新点：PRMT5放大微胶质糖酵解重编程
方法亮点：研究PRMT5与AARS1的相互作用
关键发现：阻断AARS1损害组蛋白乳酸化
insights_en: Novelty: PRMT5 amplifies microglial glycolytic reprogramming
Method highlight: Study of the interaction between PRMT5 and AARS1
Key finding: Disrupting AARS1 impairs histone lactylation
abstract: Neuropathic pain involves persistent metabolic and transcriptional remodeling in spinal microglia, but the mechanisms linking these processes remain unclear. Time-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing after chronic constriction injury identified increased PRMT5 expression in glycolysis-enriched activated microglia. Microglia-specific Prmt5 deletion or pharmacological inhibition reduced glycolytic remodeling and pain hypersensitivity. Mechanistically, PRMT5 associated with alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1 (AARS1), promoted AARS1-associated symmetric dimethylation and nuclear accumulation, and supported AARS1-dependent H3K18la and H4K12la. Disrupting AARS1 nuclear localization impaired histone lactylation and glycolytic responses. The pathway was validated in primary microglia, spinal microglia, and female mice. Chromatin profiling linked injury-associated histone lactylation to glycolytic gene programs. Finally, biomimetic siPRMT5 nanoparticles preferentially reduced PRMT5 in spinal microglia and alleviated pain hypersensitivity. These findings identify a PRMT5–AARS1–histone lactylation pathway that reinforces microglial glycolytic reprogramming and represents a potential therapeutic target for neuropathic pain.

title: Self-Supervised Uncalibrated Multi-View Video Anonymization in the Operating Room
summary_zh: 研究手术室视频匿名化，提出无需标注和校准的多视角匿名化框架。
summary_en: This study focuses on OR video anonymization, proposing a multi-view anonymization framework without annotation or calibration.
insights: 创新点：无需标注和校准的多视角匿名化框架
方法亮点：基于自监督领域自适应的单视角检测
关键发现：提高了手术室视频匿名化的效率和准确性
insights_en: Novelty: A multi-view anonymization framework without annotation or calibration
Method highlight: Self-supervised domain adaptation based on single-view detection
Key finding: Improved efficiency and accuracy of OR video anonymization
abstract: Privacy preservation is a prerequisite for using video data in Operating Room (OR) research. Effective anonymization relies on the exhaustive localization of every individual; even a single missed detection necessitates extensive manual correction. However, existing approaches face two critical scalability bottlenecks: (1) they usually require manual annotations at each new clinical site for high accuracy; (2) multi-view approaches typically require camera calibration whenever cameras are repositioned. To address these problems, we propose a self-supervised multi-view video anonymization framework based on whole-body person detection and pose estimation, without manual annotations or camera calibration. Our core strategy is to conduct self-supervised domain adaptation of a single-view detector by "retrieving" false negatives using temporal and multi-view context. We first apply an off-the-shelf wholebody detector with a low-score threshold to gather candidate detections. Then, we retrieve low-score false negatives that are consistent with high-score detections via tracking and self-supervised, uncalibrated multi-view association. The recovered detections serve as pseudo-labels to iteratively fine-tune the detector. Finally, we apply whole-body pose estimation on each detected person, and fine-tune the pose model using its own high-score predictions. Experiments on the simulated 4D-OR dataset and our real-surgery dataset achieve 99% and 97% recall, respectively. We further train a real-time whole-body detector using the generated pseudo-labels, achieving comparable performance and highlighting our method's practical applicability. Code will be available at https://github.com/CAMMA-public/ OR_anonymization.

title: Imaging in Flow and the Value of Enterprise Imaging-Sponsored by AGFA HealthCare
Bridging Graph and Pairwise Learning for Gene Regulatory Network Inference from scRNA-seq Data
summary_zh: 结合图和成对学习方法，提高基因调控网络推断的准确性。
summary_en: This paper combines graph and pairwise learning methods to improve the accuracy of GRN inference from scRNA-seq data.
insights: 创新点：融合图和成对学习方法
方法亮点：解决图方法过拟合和成对方法忽略全局结构的问题
关键发现：提高了基因调控网络推断的准确性
insights_en: Novelty: Fusion of graph and pairwise learning methods
Method highlight: Resolves overfitting in graph methods and ignoring global structure in pairwise methods
Key finding: Improved accuracy in GRN inference
abstract: MOTIVATION: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) capture the underlying interactions through which transcription factors (TFs) regulate genes. Based on gene expression data, existing GRN inference approaches generally fall into two categories: graph-based methods, which model the GRN as a whole graph, and pairwise-based methods, which decompose the GRN into individual TF-target gene pairs for modeling. However, each approach exhibits limitations that are precisely the strengths of its counterpart. Graph-based methods tend to overfit due to their reliance on a single training graph, whereas pairwise-based methods benefit from abundant TF-target training pairs. In contrast, pairwise-based methods overlook the global topological structure, which is essential for comprehensively capturing regulatory mechanisms. RESULTS: To address these limitations, we propose scGPL, an end-to-end unified framework that jointly models global regulatory topology and local interactions. scGPL extracts macro-level features from the global regulatory graph and introduces a dynamic, importance-guided subgraph sampling mechanism to capture fine-grained local dependencies. By fusing global representations with subgraph-enhanced local features, our framework bridges the gap between the two paradigms, incorporating essential whole-graph topological dependencies while retaining the data abundance advantage of pairwise methods. Extensive experiments on seven benchmark datasets demonstrate that scGPL consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance, with up to 13.7% improvement over the strongest baseline, validating the effectiveness of our integrative design. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The source code is maintained on GitHub (https://github.com/talent-hang/scGPL), and the datasets and versioned releases are archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21608485 for reproducibility.

title: MaldiSuite: a Python ecosystem for MALDI-TOF spectral processing and analysis in antimicrobial resistance research
summary_zh: 开发MaldiSuite，统一Python生态，用于MALDI-TOF光谱处理和分析。
summary_en: This paper introduces MaldiSuite, a unified Python ecosystem for MALDI-TOF spectral processing and analysis in AMR research.
insights: 创新点：统一Python生态，简化工作流程
方法亮点：基于共享数据模型和scikit-learn兼容API
关键发现：提高抗微生物耐药性研究中的诊断效率
insights_en: Novelty: A unified Python ecosystem simplifying workflows
Method highlight: Based on a shared data model and scikit-learn-compatible API
Key finding: Improved diagnostic efficiency in AMR research
abstract: MOTIVATION: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health threat requiring faster diagnostics than the 24-48 h needed for phenotypic antibiotic-susceptibility testing. Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight (MALDI-TOF) mass spectrometry is widely used in clinical microbiology for species identification but does not directly capture AMR phenotypes. Machine learning on MALDI-TOF spectra offers a promising solution, yet existing software remains fragmented across legacy R preprocessing tools and ad hoc Python scripts, lacking standardized workflows, shared application programming interfaces (APIs), and safeguards against train-test leakage. RESULTS: We present MaldiSuite, a unified Python ecosystem built on a shared data model and a scikit-learn-compatible API. It integrates three packages: MaldiAMRKit (Bruker-native and open-format input/output, standardized composable preprocessing, spectral warping, and temporal drift monitoring); MaldiBatchKit (multi-site batch correction, including MALDI-specific methods, with batch-mixing diagnostics); and MaldiDeepKit (four deep-learning classifiers: multilayer perceptron, one-dimensional convolutional neural network, residual network, and Vision Transformer). All components compose within sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline with leak-safe fit/transform semantics. On the public multi-site Database of Resistance Information on Antimicrobials and MALDI-TOF Mass Spectra (DRIAMS), MaldiSuite achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of up to 0.92 on the DRIAMS-A Staphylococcus aureus/oxacillin task, and a leakage experiment quantifies the optimistic bias that its leak-safe cross-validation removes. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: MaldiSuite is available on PyPI under the MIT licence (pip install maldisuite). Source code: https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiSuite, https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiAMRKit, https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiBatchKit, https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiDeepKit. The package versions described here and the analysis code of this paper (https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiSuite-paper), with the pinned environments, are archived at 10.5281/zenodo.24199316. DOCUMENTATION: https://ettorerocchi.github.io/MaldiSuite/. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: GSP: a multi-scale metric for evaluation of 3D RNA structure predictions
summary_zh: 提出GSP，多尺度指标评估RNA 3D结构预测。
summary_en: This paper proposes GSP, a multi-scale metric for evaluating 3D RNA structure predictions.
insights: 创新点：多尺度指标评估RNA 3D结构
方法亮点：平衡全局和局部结构差异
关键发现：提高RNA结构预测的准确性
insights_en: Novelty: Multi-scale metric for evaluating 3D RNA structures
Method highlight: Balancing global and local structural discrepancies
Key finding: Improved accuracy in RNA structure prediction
abstract: MOTIVATION: Accurate prediction of RNA 3D structures remains a central challenge in structural bioinformatics, necessitating reliable measures to quantify similarity between predicted models and experimentally determined reference structures. Currently, many scoring functions are available to assess different aspects of the tertiary structures of biomolecules. On the one hand, global measures average local irregularities, so that structures with distortions in different regions might generally be considered structurally similar. On the other hand, local conformational measures focus on specific inter-residue interactions and often fail to capture the broader topological context. Thus, there is a lack of methods capable of comprehensively assessing structural discrepancies across various spatial scales. RESULTS: To address this gap, we introduce Geometric Spherical Precision (GSP), a novel multi-scale score that assesses the quality of 3D RNA and RNP complex predictions. It integrates multiple partial scores computed from local geometric agreements into a single, easy-to-read, normalized score for ranking these predictions. We demonstrate that GSP reliably identifies models with comparable overall deviations, while maintaining strong agreement with global measures. These properties make it a useful tool for benchmarking and comparing 3D RNA structures and RNP complexes. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The GSP script and evaluation results against state-of-the-art measures on the RNA-Puzzles and CASP15 datasets are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19608328. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: SpatialMuSC: Spatial Graph-Conditioned Diffusion Refinement for Robust Spatial Multi-Omics Integration
summary_zh: 提出SpatialMuSC，用于鲁棒的空间多组学整合。
summary_en: This paper introduces SpatialMuSC, a framework for robust spatial multi-omics integration.
insights: 创新点：鲁棒的空间多组学整合框架
方法亮点：基于空间图的条件扩散细化
关键发现：提高空间多组学数据的整合质量
insights_en: Novelty: A robust spatial multi-omics integration framework
Method highlight: Spatial graph-conditioned diffusion refinement
Key finding: Improved integration quality of spatial multi-omics data
abstract: MOTIVATION: Emerging spatial multi-omics technologies enable the simultaneous profiling of multiple molecular layers within the same tissue section, offering new opportunities to interrogate tissue organization in its native spatial context. However, sequencing-derived spatial multi-omics data are often affected by intrinsic perturbations, such as technical noise, missing values, sparsity and measurement bias. These perturbations make existing methods that mainly use spatial graphs for neighborhood aggregation insufficient to recover continuous tissue-region structures, while unconstrained representation learning may propagate noisy associations and lead to fragmented spatial domains. RESULTS: We present SpatialMuSC, a robust spatial multi-omics integration framework centering on spatial graph-conditioned diffusion refinement and perturbation-invariant fusion consistency. SpatialMuSC introduces spatial topology as conditional information into the latent diffusion process, enabling spatial adjacency to guide neighborhood aggregation, spatial structure propagation and graph-aware denoising of latent states. Perturbation-invariant fusion consistency further encourages stable multi-omic fusion under perturbed observations. We evaluate SpatialMuSC on diverse spatial multi-omics datasets across different tissues and sequencing platforms, including 10x Visium, Stereo-CITE-seq, SPOTS and spatial epigenome-transcriptome data. Across these benchmarks, SpatialMuSC consistently outperforms ten state-of-the-art methods in spatial domain identification and tissue-structure preservation. Ablation analyses confirm the contributions of graph-conditioned diffusion refinement and perturbation-invariant fusion consistency, rather than post hoc graph smoothing or graph propagation alone. In particular, SpatialMuSC effectively distinguishes adjacent tissue regions, preserves block-wise smoothness and layered architectures, and shows more stable performance in missing-observation stress tests, while hippocampal marker, enrichment, and paired RNA-ATAC analyses identify a GCL-associated neuronal program and a TTR-associated accessibility feature in a choroid plexus-enriched domain. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The source code is available at https://github.com/CSUBioGroup/SpatialMuSC. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available online.

title: GLAND: Resolving small and non-continuous tissue domains via a hybrid attention mechanism
summary_zh: 开发GLAND，利用混合注意力机制解析小和非连续组织域。
summary_en: This paper presents GLAND, a framework using a hybrid attention mechanism to resolve small and non-continuous tissue domains.
insights: 创新点：混合注意力机制解析小组织域
方法亮点：空间异常检测策略优化空间图
关键发现：提高小组织域解析的准确性
insights_en: Novelty: Hybrid attention mechanism for resolving small tissue domains
Method highlight: Spatial outlier detection strategy optimizes spatial graph
Key finding: Improved accuracy in resolving small tissue domains
abstract: MOTIVATION: Recent advances in spatial transcriptomic technology provide unprecedented insights into tissue architecture by enabling high-throughput gene expression profiling with the corresponding spatial context. While identifying spatial domains is a prerequisite for understanding tissue heterogeneity and functional organization, current computational methods often fail to resolve non-continuous or small domains that, despite their biological significance, exhibit complex spatial distribution. RESULTS: We present GLAND, a deep learning framework with a hybrid attention mechanism designed to capture multi-scale spatial dependencies. GLAND utilizes a spatial outlier detection strategy to refine the spatial graph, coupled with a hybrid encoder that simultaneously captures long-range biological similarity and localized spatial continuity. Comprehensive benchmarking across 39 slices and 7 spatial transcriptomic platforms demonstrates that GLAND achieves superior performance in identifying not only traditional continuous spatial domains but also non-continuous and small domains. Within the complex tumor microenvironment, GLAND accurately resolves non-continuous tumor regions and small lymphoid aggregates. Its learned spot embeddings bridge spatial gaps by preserving the transcriptomic identity of tumor domains across distal locations, facilitating a unified characterization of heterogeneous tissue landscapes. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: GLAND is freely available at https://github.com/CSUBioGroup/GLAND. All data have been deposited to Zenodo at https://zenodo.org/records/18756215. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: ISOMPRA enables the disambiguation of transcriptional and post-transcriptional effects of genetic variants
summary_zh: 开发ISOMPRA，区分遗传变异的转录和转录后效应。
summary_en: This paper introduces ISOMPRA, an approach to distinguish transcriptional and post-transcriptional effects of genetic variants.
insights: 创新点：区分转录和转录后效应
方法亮点：ISOMPRA量化预剪接RNA和校正转录率的剪接RNA
关键发现：发现具有高影响突变的功能增强子和UTR
insights_en: Novelty: Differentiating transcriptional and post-transcriptional effects
Method highlight: ISOMPRA quantifies pre-spliced RNA and corrected spliced RNA for transcription rate
Key finding: Identified functional enhancers and UTRs with high-impact mutations
abstract: Some classic massively parallel reporter assays to study transcriptional regulatory effects of DNA sequence elements cannot readily distinguish these from post-transcriptional regulatory effects of the same element on RNA. Therefore, we developed an approach enabling assessment of DNA/RNA regulatory elements in parallel: Inferred Stability Optimized Massively Parallel Reporter Assay (ISOMPRA). ISOMPRA quantifies pre-spliced RNA to more directly assess transcription rate, and spliced RNA, corrected for transcription rate, to identify RNA stability-altering 3′-UTR elements. We benchmark ISOMPRA with both predicted enhancers and 3′-UTR elements, including regions containing autism patient mutations. We identify numerous functional enhancers and UTRs and discover a subset with high-impact mutations. We further show that failing to consider both potential transcriptional and post-transcriptional effects results in numerous possible false positives and false negatives. Finally, we adapt ISOMPRA for cell-type-specific in vivo use, enabling analyses of variants in specific cell types in the brain and measurement of regulatory impacts of in vivo traits, such as sex.

Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Review
summary_zh: 肥厚型心肌病是一种左心室肥厚疾病，常见于无瓣膜病、高血压或其他慢性疾病的人群。
summary_en: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a condition characterized by left ventricular hypertrophy, commonly found in individuals without valvular disease, uncontrolled hypertension, or other chronic conditions.
insights: 肥厚型心肌病的定义和发病率
诊断方法为超声心动图
与猝死风险相关
insights_en: Definition and incidence of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Diagnosis by echocardiography
Association with sudden death risk
abstract: Importance: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is defined as left ventricular hypertrophy of greater than 15 mm in any part of the left ventricular wall in the absence of valvular disease, uncontrolled hypertension, or other chronic conditions causing severe left ventricular hypertrophy such as uncontrolled hypertension or cardiac amyloidosis. Most people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy have a normal lifespan; however, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is associated with a 0.8% annual incidence of sudden cardiac death. Observations: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy affects an estimated 0.2% of people worldwide (including more than 600 000 people in the US) and is typically diagnosed with echocardiography. Approximately 35% to 40% of patients report effort-related dyspnea, chest pain or pressure, or lightheadedness. Approximately 30% to 40% of people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy have a pathogenic gene variant that encodes for cardiac sarcomere proteins (predominantly myosin binding protein C, myosin heavy chain, and troponin). Other patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy may have a polygenic predisposition and/or nongenetic risk factors. The sarcomeric gene variants cause hypercontractility and delayed relaxation of the cardiac sarcomere, which characterizes the underlying pathophysiologic problem in people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Approximately 60% to 70% of patients have obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, characterized by dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to basal septal hypertrophy. The remainder do not have outflow tract obstruction and, therefore, have nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy should participate in regular low- to moderate-intensity physical activity (such as brisk walking, jogging) as part of a healthy lifestyle. Medical therapies such as β-blockers (eg, metoprolol, bisoprolol, nadolol) and nondihydropyridine-class calcium channel blockers (eg, verapamil or diltiazem) are first-line medical therapy for patients with symptoms due to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. If first-line therapies do not relieve symptoms, alternative treatments include disopyramide, which improves symptoms in approximately 60% of patients, cardiac myosin inhibitors (mavacamten or aficamten), which improve symptoms in approximately 70% to 80% of patients, or procedures to thin the septal wall of the left ventricle, including percutaneous alcohol septal ablation, which improves symptoms in approximately 75% to 80% of patients, or surgical septal myectomy, which improves symptoms in approximately 90% to 95% of patients. Guidelines recommend that first-degree relatives of patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy undergo screening for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with genetic testing or echocardiography. Conclusions: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is caused by a monogenetic pathogenic variant in approximately 30% to 40% of patients and can cause effort-related dyspnea, chest pain or pressure, or lightheadedness. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is associated with an incidence of sudden cardiac death of 0.8% per year. First-line therapies for symptomatic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy are β-blockers (eg, metoprolol, bisoprolol, nadolol) or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (eg, verapamil, diltiazem).

title: Prehospital Fluid Resuscitation for Patients With Suspected Sepsis: The PITSTOP-Fluids Factorial Randomized Clinical Trial
summary_zh: 研究早期静脉输液对疑似败血症患者死亡率的影响。
summary_en: This study determines the effect of early intravenous fluid resuscitation on mortality in patients with suspected sepsis.
insights: 早期静脉输液对败血症患者的效果
多中心随机临床试验设计
对临床实践的指导意义
insights_en: Effect of early intravenous fluid resuscitation on sepsis patients
Design of a multicenter randomized clinical trial
Guidance for clinical practice
abstract: Importance: Early resuscitation with intravenous fluids is recommended for patients with sepsis. Objective: To determine the effect of liberal vs more conservative fluid resuscitation strategies in the ambulance on mortality among patients with suspected sepsis. Design, Setting, and Participants: Multicenter, 2 × 2 factorial randomized clinical trial conducted by 4 paramedic services and their destination hospitals in Ontario, Canada. Participants were adults with suspected sepsis, defined as suspected infection, fever (≥38.0 °C), and hypotension (systolic blood pressure [SBP] <100 mm Hg), and obtainable intravenous access. Patients were enrolled between March 23, 2020, and August 20, 2025, with last follow-up in December 2025. Intervention: Patients were randomized to receive liberal fluids (up to 2 L of normal saline regardless of subsequent SBP) or usual care (fluids only when SBP <90 mm Hg and stopped when SBP ≥100 mm Hg) during prehospital care and until transfer of care in the emergency department. (Patients were additionally randomized to receive ceftriaxone vs placebo; analysis of which is reported separately.). Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcome was hospital mortality, defined as death prior to hospital discharge up to day 90. There were 17 secondary outcomes, including all-cause mortality at 90 days, hospitalization, intensive care unit admission, mechanical ventilation, vasopressor therapy, dialysis, and total fluids infused within 24 hours of hospital arrival. Results: Among 1686 randomized patients, 1669 were eligible and 1646 were included in the primary outcome analysis (830 in the liberal fluids group and 816 in the usual fluids group). The median age of patients was 76 (IQR, 63-85) years and 938 (57.0%) were male. Most patients in both groups received a fluid bolus (826/848 [97.4%] in the liberal fluids group; 700/821 [85.3%] in the usual fluids group) during transport, but patients in the liberal fluids group received a larger volume (median, 1500 mL [IQR, 1000-2000 mL]) vs 500 mL [IQR, 175-800 mL] in the usual fluids group; difference, 910.1 mL [95% CI, 857.3-962.9 mL]). Hospital mortality was 149/830 (18.0%) in the liberal fluids group and 149/816 (18.3%) in the usual fluids group (risk ratio, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.80-1.20]; unadjusted risk difference, -0.3 [95% CI, -4.0 to 3.4]; P = .82). Among the 17 secondary outcomes, all were similar between groups. Adverse events, including pulmonary edema during transport, were infrequent in both groups. Conclusions and Relevance: A more liberal fluid resuscitation strategy for the prehospital management of patients with suspected sepsis did not reduce mortality compared with more restrictive usual care. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03068741.

Guidance for clinical practice
abstract: Importance: Early treatment with antibiotics is considered an important intervention to reduce mortality for patients with sepsis. Objective: To determine the effect of earlier treatment with antibiotics in the ambulance on 90-day mortality compared with usual treatment in the emergency department. Design, Setting, and Participants: This multicenter, 2 × 2 factorial randomized, placebo-controlled trial was conducted among 4 paramedic services and their destination hospitals in Ontario, Canada. Participants were adults with suspected sepsis, defined as suspected infection, fever (≥38.0 °C), and hypotension (systolic blood pressure <100 mm Hg). Patients were enrolled between March 23, 2020, and August 20, 2025, with final follow-up in December 2025. Interventions: Patients were randomized to receive 1 g of intramuscular ceftriaxone or placebo (and to receive liberal fluids vs usual fluids; reported separately) during prehospital care in the ambulance. All patients could receive open-label antibiotics in the emergency department. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcome was hospital mortality, defined as death prior to hospital discharge to day 90. There were 17 secondary outcomes, including all-cause mortality at 90 days, hospitalization, intensive care unit admission, use of mechanical ventilation, use of dialysis, positive culture results, and antibiotics within 24 hours of hospital arrival. Results: Among 2091 randomized patients, 2048 were eligible for the primary analysis, with 1026 randomized to receive ceftriaxone and 1022 randomized to receive placebo. The median (IQR) age of patients was 75 (62-85) years and 1162 (56.7%) were males. The mean (SD) time from paramedic arrival at patient to administration of study drug was 37 (36) minutes in the ceftriaxone group and 39 (55) minutes in the placebo group. Most patients (735 of 795 [92.5%] in the ceftriaxone group and 730 of 792 [92.2%] in placebo group) were treated with antibiotics in the hospital after a mean (SD) of 247.3 (207.7) minutes after paramedic arrival among patients in the ceftriaxone group and 252.8 (218.0) minutes among the placebo group. The rate of hospital mortality was 182 of 1009 (18.0%) in the ceftriaxone group and 186 of 1011 (18.4%) in the placebo group (risk ratio, 0.97 [95% CI, 0.81-1.17]; P = .77). Of 17 secondary outcomes, all were similar between the groups. Conclusions and Relevance: Among patients with suspected sepsis on evaluation by paramedics, earlier treatment with antibiotics in the ambulance did not reduce mortality compared with usual care provided in the emergency department. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03068741.

insights_en: Comparison of olanzapine and droperidol in efficacy
Design of a randomized clinical trial
Guidance for treating behavioral disturbances in children and adolescents
abstract: Importance: Acute behavioral disturbance is a high-risk emergency department presentation. There is limited evidence for the comparative effectiveness of intramuscular sedative medications in children and adolescents, which may be required when there is imminent risk of serious harm due to agitation. Objective: To determine whether olanzapine is more effective than droperidol intramuscularly in achieving behavioral containment. Design, Setting, and Participants: This investigator-initiated, open-label, multicenter, superiority, randomized clinical trial recruited children and adolescents aged 9 to 17 years presenting to 10 Australian emergency departments with acute behavioral disturbance clinically deemed to require intramuscular medication from November 8, 2021, to February 16, 2026. The last participant follow-up occurred on March 17, 2026. Data were analyzed from April 15 to 27, 2026. Interventions: Participants were randomly assigned to a single weight-based dose of olanzapine or droperidol (<40 kg, 5 mg; ≥40 kg, 10 mg). Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcome was successful sedation (Sedation Assessment Tool score ≤0) without the need for additional sedatives 1 hour after randomization. A range of secondary outcomes, including adverse events, were assessed. Results: Of 348 recruited individuals (mean [IQR] age, 14.9 [13.6-16.1] years; 215 [62%] female; 75 Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander individuals), 176 were assigned to olanzapine and 172 to droperidol. Of those randomized, 117 individuals (66%) in the olanzapine group and 121 individuals (70%) in the droperidol group were administered their study medication within 30 minutes of randomization. Successful sedation without the requirement for additional sedatives occurred in 89 individuals (53%) in the olanzapine group and 104 individuals (62%) in the droperidol group. No evidence of superiority was observed (adjusted risk difference, -8.3% [95% CI, -18.6% to 2.1%]; P = .12). One serious adverse event (apnea) occurred in the olanzapine group. Conclusions and Relevance: In this randomized clinical trial in children and adolescents presenting to the emergency department with behavioral disturbance, intramuscular olanzapine did not result in a clinically meaningfully greater proportion achieving successful sedation compared with droperidol. The limited effectiveness observed with both medications highlights the need for more effective pharmacological and nonpharmacological management strategies. title: A Trial for Pediatric Agitation in the Emergency Department—New Calm in the Chaos
VUOD: A Versatile Unsupervised Outlier Detection Framework for Natural, Industrial, Medical Images and Beyond
summary_zh: 提出一种通用的无监督异常检测框架，适用于自然、工业、医学图像等领域。
summary_en: This work introduces a versatile unsupervised outlier detection framework applicable to natural, industrial, medical images, and beyond.
insights: 通用无监督异常检测框架的提出
特征判别性改进
在多个领域和基准数据集上的性能
insights_en: Proposal of a versatile unsupervised outlier detection framework
Improvement of feature discriminativeness
Performance across multiple domains and benchmark datasets
abstract: Unsupervised outlier detection that automatically identifies whether visual systems involve anomalous images is a significant research topic. However, most approaches are limited to natural images because they rely on frozen and pre-trained feature extractors. So that their performance cannot be maintained in practical scenarios, especially for industrial inspection and medical imaging. In this work, we first revisit this task and then introduce a versatile unsupervised outlier detection framework to enrich the application domains. The core idea of this framework is to improve feature discriminativess via exploiting intrinsic distribution priors. Evaluated on 3 domains and 14 benchmark datasets, our proposed solution achieves state-of-the-art performance and significantly outperforms existing methods. More importantly, we show its plug-and-play property that can be integrated into diverse visual applications to improve their robustness, such as image classification and 3D reconstruction.

title: CrownFusion: 3D Dental Crown Generation Using Geometry Images and Latent Diffusion
summary_zh: 本文提出CrownFusion，利用几何图像和潜在扩散模型生成3D牙冠设计。实验表明，该方法能生成符合个体病例的牙冠。
summary_en: This paper introduces CrownFusion, a method for generating 3D dental crown designs using geometry images and latent diffusion models. Experiments show that this method can generate crowns tailored to individual patient cases.
insights: 创新点：利用几何图像和潜在扩散模型生成牙冠
方法亮点：生成符合个体病例的牙冠
关键发现：CrownFusion在牙冠生成中表现良好
insights_en: Novelty: Generating crowns using geometry images and latent diffusion models
Method highlight: Generating crowns tailored to individual patient cases
Key finding: CrownFusion performs well in crown generation
abstract: We introduce CrownFusion, a latent diffusion model to generate 3D dental crown designs from geometry images, a 2D-grid encoding of surface coordinates. Departing from traditional approaches that use point clouds, our"CrownImage"representation not only unlocks the full power of image-based generative architectures, but also preserves fine geometric detail by operating at far higher spatial resolutions than point clouds to alleviate smoothing artifacts in the 3D generation. Conditioned on jointly learned embeddings of the surrounding dentition, our probabilistic diffusion model produces anatomically plausible crowns with morphological variations tailored to individual patient cases. To accommodate multiple valid designs, we propose an occlusal fit metric based on proximity to the antagonist teeth. We evaluate our method through quantitative experiments and qualitative studies involving expert testimonials. We also release the FDI 16 Crown Dataset, comprising 11,513 annotated intra-oral scans, to support future research in dental CAD.
